    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- next: Goes on a slide.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- indicator: A button for one slide.
    - `data-current`: Present on the slide the view is at, and on its button.

### Checkbox

```
import { Checkbox } from "@kirana-ui/react/checkbox"
```

Parts: `<Checkbox.Root>`, `<Checkbox.Indicator>`.

Anatomy:

```
<Checkbox.Root>
  <Checkbox.Indicator>
```

Props of its root:

- `checked?: boolean`: Whether it is checked, when the caller holds it.
- `defaultChecked?: boolean`: Read once.
- `onCheckedChange?: (checked: boolean, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Heard as it is about to be checked or unchecked: `details.cancel()` keeps it as it was.
- `disabled?: boolean`: Disabled: it cannot be changed.
- `readOnly?: boolean`: Shown as it is, focusable, not changeable.
- `required?: boolean`: Needed: in a `Field`, leaving it unchecked is then invalid.
- `name?: string`: With a name, the control is submitted with the form around it when it is checked.
- `form?: string`: The id of the form the control belongs to, when it is not inside it.
- `value?: string`: What is submitted. Default `"on"`, as a native checkbox's.
- `indeterminate?: boolean`: Neither checked nor unchecked: a parent of boxes that disagree.
- `parent?: boolean`: In a checkbox group with `allValues`: the box that stands for them all, written anywhere inside the group. It is checked when every one is, mixed when some are, and it is not submitted; its `aria-controls` names the boxes. A press from mixed checks them all, the next unchecks them all, and the next brings back the set they were left in (left all checked or none, a press goes between all and none); a disabled box keeps its state. Read once.
- `id?: string`: The id of the box's hidden native checkbox, not of the box: a `<label for>` names it. Inside a `Field`, that input takes the field's id instead.

Each part, and its own props:

- `<Checkbox.Root>` draws a `<span>`. Its props are above.
- `<Checkbox.Indicator>` draws a `<span>`. A dash while mixed and a tick while checked, from the part's state: `<Checkbox.Indicator render={(props, state) => <span {...props}>{state.indeterminate ? "–" : "✓"}</span>} />`.
    - `keepMounted?: boolean`: Keeps the mark in the page while the box is unchecked.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: The box. It holds a hidden native checkbox, which a form and a label reach.
    - `data-checked`: Present when it is checked.
    - `data-unchecked`: Present when it is not checked.
    - `data-indeterminate`: Present when it is neither checked nor unchecked.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when the form needs it.
    - `data-parent`: Present on the checkbox that stands for every box of its group.
- indicator: The mark. In the page while the box is checked or indeterminate. `data-indeterminate` and `data-checked` say which mark to draw, a dash or a tick: in CSS (`[data-indeterminate]`), or from the part's state. Through its exit the box is already unchecked, and both are absent.
    - `data-checked`: Present when it is checked.
    - `data-unchecked`: Present when it is not checked.
    - `data-indeterminate`: Present when it is neither checked nor unchecked.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when the form needs it.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.

### CheckboxGroup

```
import { CheckboxGroup } from "@kirana-ui/react/checkbox-group"
```

Props:

- `value?: readonly string[]`: The values of the checked checkboxes, when the caller holds them.
- `defaultValue?: readonly string[]`: The values checked at the start, when the caller does not hold `value`. Read once.
- `onValueChange?: (value: string[], details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Heard as a checkbox of the group is about to be checked or unchecked, with the values that would then be checked: `details.cancel()` keeps them as they were.
- `allValues?: readonly string[]`: The value of every checkbox of the group, for a checkbox marked `parent`: it is checked when all of them are, mixed when some are, and a press on it goes from the set they were left in to all, then none, then back. Its order names the boxes' elements (`<id>-0` …).
- `disabled?: boolean`: Disables every checkbox of the group.
- `id?: string`: The group's own id, and what its boxes' elements are named from (`<id>-0`, `<id>-1` …, by their place in `allValues`), which a parent box's `aria-controls` names. Inside a `Field`, the group takes the field's id instead.

`<CheckboxGroup>` draws a `<div>`.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: The group: `role="group"`, with its `id`. Name it with `aria-label`, or `aria-labelledby` naming a heading of your own; inside a `Field`, the field's label names it and its description describes it. A checkbox anywhere inside it with a `value` is checked while the group's value holds it; one marked `parent`, anywhere inside it too, stands for every value of `allValues`, and its `aria-controls` names their boxes.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.

### Collapsible

```
import { Collapsible } from "@kirana-ui/react/collapsible"
```

Parts: `<Collapsible.Root>`, `<Collapsible.Trigger>`, `<Collapsible.Panel>`.

Anatomy:

```
<Collapsible.Root>
  <Collapsible.Trigger> (repeated)
  <Collapsible.Panel>
```

Props of its root:

- `open?: boolean`: Whether it is open, when the caller holds it.
- `defaultOpen?: boolean`: Read once.
- `onOpenChange?: (open: boolean, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Heard as it is about to open or close: `details.cancel()` keeps it as it was.
- `disabled?: boolean`: Disabled: its trigger does not open or close it.

Each part, and its own props:

- `<Collapsible.Root>` draws a `<div>`. Its props are above.
- `<Collapsible.Trigger>` draws a `<button>`.
- `<Collapsible.Panel>` draws a `<div>`.
    - `keepMounted?: boolean`: Keeps the closed panel in the page, `hidden`.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: Groups the trigger and the panel.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- trigger: The button that opens and closes the panel.
    - `data-panel-open`: Present when the panel is open.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- panel: The content. In the page while open, and through its exit's motion.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
    - `--collapsible-panel-height`: The panel's content height while it opens or closes, `auto` once it is open.
    - `--collapsible-panel-width`: The panel's content width while it opens or closes, `auto` once it is open.

### Combobox

```
import { Combobox } from "@kirana-ui/react/combobox"
```

Parts: `<Combobox.Root>`, `<Combobox.Input>`, `<Combobox.Trigger>`, `<Combobox.Value>`, `<Combobox.Clear>`, `<Combobox.Chips>`, `<Combobox.Chip>`, `<Combobox.ChipRemove>`, `<Combobox.Portal>`, `<Combobox.Positioner>`, `<Combobox.Popup>`, `<Combobox.List>`, `<Combobox.Collection>`, `<Combobox.Group>`, `<Combobox.GroupLabel>`, `<Combobox.Separator>`, `<Combobox.Item>`, `<Combobox.ItemIndicator>`, `<Combobox.Empty>`, `<Combobox.Status>`.

Anatomy:

```
<Combobox.Root>
  <Combobox.Input>
  <Combobox.Trigger>
    <Combobox.Value> (optional)
  <Combobox.Portal>
    <Combobox.Positioner>
      <Combobox.Popup>
        <Combobox.Input> (as above)
        <Combobox.List> (optional)
          <Combobox.Collection> (optional)
            <Combobox.Item> (repeated, as above)
            <Combobox.Group> (optional, repeated, as above)
          <Combobox.Group> (optional, repeated)
            <Combobox.Collection> (optional, as above)
            <Combobox.Item> (repeated)
              <Combobox.ItemIndicator>
            <Combobox.GroupLabel>
          <Combobox.Separator> (repeated)
        <Combobox.Collection> (optional, as above)
        <Combobox.Empty>
        <Combobox.Status> (optional)
  <Combobox.Popup> (as above)
  <Combobox.Status> (optional, as above)
  <Combobox.Clear>
  <Combobox.Chips>
    <Combobox.Input> (as above)
    <Combobox.Chip> (repeated)
      <Combobox.ChipRemove>
```

Props of its root:

- `value?: Value | null`: The chosen value; `null` is "none".
- `defaultValue?: Value | null`: The value it starts with, when the caller does not hold `value`. Read once.
- `onValueChange?: (value: Value | null, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Heard as a value is about to be chosen or cleared: `details.cancel()` keeps it as it was.
- `inputValue?: string`: What the input says.
- `defaultInputValue?: string`: The text the input starts with, when the caller does not hold `inputValue`. Read once.
- `onInputValueChange?: (value: string, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Heard as the input's text is about to change: `details.cancel()` keeps it as it was.
- `open?: boolean`: Whether the list is open, when the caller holds it.
- `defaultOpen?: boolean`: Whether the list starts open, when the caller does not hold `open`. Read once.
- `onOpenChange?: (open: boolean, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Heard as the list is about to open or close: `details.cancel()` keeps it as it was.
- `disabled?: boolean`: Disabled: it cannot be changed.
- `readOnly?: boolean`: Its value can be read and not changed. The list still opens and can be gone through, by the pointer and the arrows, but no press and no Enter chooses; nothing typed is taken, and its clear and chip buttons do nothing. It keeps focus, and its value is still submitted.
- `name?: string`: With a name, the value is submitted with the form around it.
- `form?: string`: The id of the form the control belongs to, when it is not inside it.
- `items?: readonly ComboboxItemData<Value>[] | readonly ComboboxGroupData<Value>[] | Readonly<Record<string, string>>`: The values with their labels: a list of them, groups of them (`{ value, items }`, `value` the group's name), or, for values that are text, the labels by value (`{ apple: "Apple" }`). The input shows a value by its label from here before the list has ever been opened. With the items written in the markup that is all it is for. With a `Collection` it is the list itself: the combobox filters it by what is typed, and the `Collection` draws what is left.
- `filter?: ((label: string, query: string) => boolean) | null`: Whether an item is shown for what was typed. Default: its label holds the text, without regard to case. `null`: every item is shown, and the caller draws the ones it wants (or gives the `items` it wants, when they are loaded for what was typed).
- `multiple?: boolean`: Several values, each shown as a chip beside the input: an item chosen is added, chosen again taken away, and the list stays open. The values are `values`, not `value`.
- `values?: readonly Value[]`: With `multiple`: the chosen values, in the order they were chosen.
- `defaultValues?: readonly Value[]`: With `multiple`: the values it starts with, when the caller does not hold `values`. Read once.
- `onValuesChange?: (values: Value[], details: ChangeDetails) => void`: With `multiple`: heard as a value is about to be added or taken away, with the values there would then be: `details.cancel()` keeps them as they were.
- `required?: boolean`: In a field, "none" is then wrong.
- `inline?: boolean`: The list is always in the page, under the input, with no popup: a command palette. An item chosen is told to the caller, and the input keeps what was typed.
- `virtualized?: ListCollection`: Every row, when only some are in the page (a virtualizer draws the ones in view). The caller then filters: the collection is what is left, and each item is given its `index`.
- `autoHighlight?: boolean`: The first item shown for what was typed is highlighted as one types, so Enter chooses it. Off by default: typing then highlights nothing, and Enter chooses once an arrow or the pointer has gone to an item. Either way a list opened with nothing typed is on its chosen item, if it has one.

Each part, and its own props:

- `<Combobox.Root>` draws no element. Generic: `<Value = unknown>`. `Value` is what tells an item from the others: the type of `value`, and of `values`' entries. Its props are above.
- `<Combobox.Input>` draws a `<input>`.
- `<Combobox.Trigger>` draws a `<button>`.
- `<Combobox.Value>` draws no element. Generic: `<Chosen = unknown>`. The chosen value's label, or a placeholder while nothing is chosen, for a button that is the combobox (its input inside the popup). With several values, their labels with commas between.
    - `placeholder?: ReactNode`: Shown while nothing is chosen.
    - `children?: ReactNode | (( value: Chosen, label: Chosen extends readonly unknown[] ? readonly string[] : string | undefined ) => ReactNode)`: What to show in place of the label. A function is given the value and its label (`null` and `undefined` while nothing is chosen); with `multiple`, the values and their labels, in the order they were chosen.
- `<Combobox.Clear>` draws a `<button>`.
    - `keepMounted?: boolean`: Keeps the button in the page while there is nothing to clear.
- `<Combobox.Chips>` draws a `<div>`. With several values: what holds the chips and the input, and what the list is placed against.
- `<Combobox.Chip>` draws a `<span>`. One chosen value.
    - `value: unknown`: Required. The chosen value this chip stands for.
- `<Combobox.ChipRemove>` draws a `<button>`.
- `<Combobox.Portal>` draws no element. Draws no element of its own: its children at the end of `<body>`, or where a `PortalProvider` says.
- `<Combobox.Positioner>` draws a `<div>`. Takes the positioner options ("Positioner options", above).
- `<Combobox.Popup>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<Combobox.List>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<Combobox.Collection>` draws no element. Generic: `<Value = unknown>`. Draws the list from the root's `items`: its content once for each item left for what was typed, or for each group that has items left; given a group, for each of that group's items left. The root then filters, and no item hides itself.
    - `of?: ComboboxEntry<Value>`: A group the root's `items` gave: its items left are then what is drawn.
    - `children: (entry: ComboboxEntry<Value>) => ReactNode`: Required. Drawn once for each item left, or for each group that has items left.
- `<Combobox.Group>` draws a `<div>`. Items that belong together, named by their label. Hidden while none is shown.
- `<Combobox.GroupLabel>` draws a `<div>`. The name of a group. Outside a group it is plain text, and names nothing.
- `<Combobox.Separator>` draws a `<div>`. A line between groups.
- `<Combobox.Item>` draws a `<div>`.
    - `value: unknown`: Required. What the combobox's value is while this item is chosen.
    - `disabled?: boolean`: Disables this item: it cannot be chosen, and the arrows pass over it.
    - `label?: string`: What is filtered and what the input shows; the item's text when left out.
    - `index?: number`: Its place among all the rows, in a virtualized list.
- `<Combobox.ItemIndicator>` draws a `<span>`. A mark an item shows while it is the chosen one.
    - `keepMounted?: boolean`: Keeps the mark in the page while its item is not chosen.
- `<Combobox.Empty>` draws a `<div>`. What is shown when no item is.
- `<Combobox.Status>` draws a `<div>`. Says how the list stands ("3 results", "Loading") to software that reads the page, as its text changes. It stays in the page while its text changes: inside the popup, or beside the input.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- input: The text input. What is typed filters the list, which is placed against it, or against the chips' box when it is in one. Inside the popup, it takes focus while the popup is open.
    - `data-popup-open`: Present when the list is open.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
- trigger: A button that opens and closes the list. With the input inside the popup it is the combobox: a stop for Tab, and what the popup is placed against.
    - `data-popup-open`: Present when the list is open.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
- positioner: Places the list against the input: against the chips' box when the input is in one, the button when the input is inside the popup, or its own `anchor`. It carries the geometry.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `--anchor-width`: The anchor's width.
    - `--anchor-height`: The anchor's height.
    - `--available-width`: The width between the anchor and the edge of the viewport.
    - `--available-height`: The height between the anchor and the edge of the viewport.
    - `--transform-origin`: The point of the popup nearest its anchor, to scale from.
- popup: The list of items. With a `list` inside, what holds it: a dialog around an input and the list.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `data-empty`: Present when no item is shown for what was typed.
- list: The items' own box inside the popup, when the popup holds more than items (an input): it is then the listbox.
    - `data-empty`: Present when no item is shown for what was typed.
- item: One choice in the list.
    - `data-selected`: Present on the chosen item.
    - `data-highlighted`: Present on the item the pointer or the keyboard is on.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- clear: A button that empties the input and the value.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- chipRemove: A chip's button that takes its value away.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.

### Command

```
import { Command } from "@kirana-ui/react/command"
```

Parts: `<Command.Root>`, `<Command.Input>`, `<Command.List>`, `<Command.Empty>`, `<Command.Group>`, `<Command.GroupHeading>`, `<Command.Item>`, `<Command.Separator>`.

Anatomy:

```
<Command.Root>
  <Command.Input>
  <Command.List>
    <Command.Empty>
    <Command.Group> (optional, repeated)
      <Command.GroupHeading>
      <Command.Item> (repeated)
    <Command.Separator> (repeated)
```

Props of its root:

- `inputValue?: string`: What the input says.
- `defaultInputValue?: string`: The text the input starts with, when the caller does not hold `inputValue`. Read once. Default `""`.
- `onInputValueChange?: (value: string, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Heard as the input's text is about to change: `details.cancel()` keeps it as it was.
- `onSelect?: (value: string, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: An item was chosen: pressed, or Enter while it was highlighted.
- `filter?: ((label: string, query: string, keywords: readonly string[]) => boolean) | null`: Whether an item is shown for what was typed. Default: its label or one of its keywords holds the text, without regard to case. `null`: every item is shown, and the caller draws the ones it wants.
- `loop?: boolean`: Whether a step past an end of the list goes round to the other.
- `disabled?: boolean`: Disabled: nothing can be typed or chosen.
- `autoHighlight?: boolean`: Whether the first item shown is highlighted from the start and again whenever the text changes, so Enter does it with no arrow key first, as a command palette is used. Default: `true`. With `false`, nothing is highlighted until the input has focus or an arrow or the pointer moves to an item.

Each part, and its own props:

- `<Command.Root>` draws a `<div>`. Its props are above.
- `<Command.Input>` draws a `<input>`.
- `<Command.List>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<Command.Empty>` draws a `<div>`. What is shown when no item is.
- `<Command.Group>` draws a `<div>`. Items under a heading. Hidden while none of them is shown.
- `<Command.GroupHeading>` draws a `<div>`. A group's name.
- `<Command.Item>` draws a `<div>`.
    - `value: string`: Required. What `onSelect` is told.
    - `disabled?: boolean`: Disables this item: it cannot be chosen, and the arrows pass over it.
    - `label?: string`: What is filtered; the item's text when left out.
    - `keywords?: readonly string[]`: Other words the item answers to.
- `<Command.Separator>` draws a `<div>`. A line between groups. Hidden while something is typed.
    - `alwaysRender?: boolean`: Stays while something is typed.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: A list of commands with the input that filters it.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- input: The text input. What is typed filters the list; focus stays in it.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- list: The commands.
    - `data-empty`: Present when no item is shown for what was typed.
- item: One command.
    - `data-highlighted`: Present on the item the pointer or the keyboard is on.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.

### ContextMenu

```
import { ContextMenu } from "@kirana-ui/react/context-menu"
```

Parts: `<ContextMenu.Root>`, `<ContextMenu.Trigger>`, `<ContextMenu.Portal>`, `<ContextMenu.Positioner>`, `<ContextMenu.Popup>`, `<ContextMenu.Arrow>`, `<ContextMenu.Item>`, `<ContextMenu.LinkItem>`, `<ContextMenu.Group>`, `<ContextMenu.GroupLabel>`, `<ContextMenu.Separator>`, `<ContextMenu.CheckboxItem>`, `<ContextMenu.CheckboxItemIndicator>`, `<ContextMenu.RadioGroup>`, `<ContextMenu.RadioItem>`, `<ContextMenu.RadioItemIndicator>`, `<ContextMenu.SubmenuRoot>`, `<ContextMenu.SubmenuTrigger>`.

Anatomy:

```
<ContextMenu.Root>
  <ContextMenu.Trigger>
  <ContextMenu.Portal>
    <ContextMenu.Positioner>
      <ContextMenu.Popup>
        <ContextMenu.Arrow>
        <ContextMenu.Group> (optional, repeated)
          <ContextMenu.Item> (repeated)
          <ContextMenu.LinkItem> (repeated)
          <ContextMenu.GroupLabel>
          <ContextMenu.CheckboxItem> (repeated)
            <ContextMenu.CheckboxItemIndicator>
          <ContextMenu.RadioGroup> (repeated)
            <ContextMenu.RadioItem> (repeated)
              <ContextMenu.RadioItemIndicator>
          <ContextMenu.SubmenuRoot> (repeated)
            <ContextMenu.Portal> (as above)
            <ContextMenu.SubmenuTrigger>
        <ContextMenu.Separator> (repeated)
```

Props of its root:

- `open?: boolean`: Whether it is open, when the caller holds it.
- `defaultOpen?: boolean`: Whether it starts open, when the caller does not hold `open`. Read once.
- `onOpenChange?: (open: boolean, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Heard as it is about to open or close: `details.cancel()` keeps it as it was.
- `disabled?: boolean`: The trigger cannot be pressed; a submenu's is passed over.
- `loop?: boolean`: Whether the arrows go round from the last item to the first. Default: they do.
- `modal?: boolean`: Holds the page while the menu is open: its scroll is locked, and a press outside closes the menu and reaches nothing. Default: it does not. Not for a submenu.

Each part, and its own props:

- `<ContextMenu.Root>` draws no element. Holds the menu: whether it is open. Its props are above.
- `<ContextMenu.Trigger>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<ContextMenu.Portal>` draws no element. Draws no element of its own: its children at the end of `<body>`, or where a `PortalProvider` says.
- `<ContextMenu.Positioner>` draws a `<div>`. Takes the positioner options ("Positioner options", above).
- `<ContextMenu.Popup>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<ContextMenu.Arrow>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<ContextMenu.Item>` draws a `<div>`.
    - `disabled?: boolean`: Disables this item: it cannot be pressed, and the arrows pass over it.
    - `label?: string`: What typing matches; the item's text when left out.
    - `closeOnClick?: boolean`: Whether choosing the item closes the menu. Default: it does for an item, and does not for a checkbox or a radio item.
- `<ContextMenu.LinkItem>` draws a `<a>`.
    - `disabled?: boolean`: Disables this item: it cannot be pressed, and the arrows pass over it.
    - `label?: string`: What typing matches; the item's text when left out.
    - `closeOnClick?: boolean`: Whether choosing the item closes the menu. Default: it does for an item, and does not for a checkbox or a radio item.
- `<ContextMenu.Group>` draws a `<div>`. Items that belong together, named by their label.
- `<ContextMenu.GroupLabel>` draws a `<div>`. The name of a group. Outside a group it is plain text, and names nothing.
- `<ContextMenu.Separator>` draws a `<div>`. A line between items.
- `<ContextMenu.CheckboxItem>` draws a `<div>`.
    - `disabled?: boolean`: Disables this item: it cannot be pressed, and the arrows pass over it.
    - `label?: string`: What typing matches; the item's text when left out.
    - `closeOnClick?: boolean`: Whether choosing the item closes the menu. Default: it does for an item, and does not for a checkbox or a radio item.
    - `checked?: boolean`: Whether the item is checked, when the caller holds it.
    - `defaultChecked?: boolean`: Whether the item starts checked, when the caller does not hold `checked`. Read once.
    - `onCheckedChange?: (checked: boolean, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Heard as the item is about to be checked or unchecked: `details.cancel()` keeps it as it was.
- `<ContextMenu.CheckboxItemIndicator>` draws a `<span>`.
    - `keepMounted?: boolean`: Keeps the mark in the page while its item is not checked.
- `<ContextMenu.RadioGroup>` draws a `<div>`. Generic: `<Value = unknown>`. `Value` is what tells a radio item from the others: the type of `value`.
    - `value?: Value | null`: The chosen value; `null` is "none".
    - `defaultValue?: Value | null`: The value it starts with, when the caller does not hold `value`. Read once.
    - `onValueChange?: (value: Value, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Told an item's own value, never `null`: a press chooses, and nothing takes the choice back.
    - `disabled?: boolean`: Disables every item of the group.
- `<ContextMenu.RadioItem>` draws a `<div>`.
    - `disabled?: boolean`: Disables this item: it cannot be pressed, and the arrows pass over it.
    - `label?: string`: What typing matches; the item's text when left out.
    - `closeOnClick?: boolean`: Whether choosing the item closes the menu. Default: it does for an item, and does not for a checkbox or a radio item.
    - `value: unknown`: Required. What the radio group's value is while this item is the chosen one.
- `<ContextMenu.RadioItemIndicator>` draws a `<span>`.
    - `keepMounted?: boolean`: Keeps the mark in the page while its item is not checked.
- `<ContextMenu.SubmenuRoot>` draws no element. A submenu: it holds the item that opens it and a portal, positioner and popup of its own.
    - `open?: boolean`: Whether it is open, when the caller holds it.
    - `defaultOpen?: boolean`: Whether it starts open, when the caller does not hold `open`. Read once.
    - `onOpenChange?: (open: boolean, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Heard as it is about to open or close: `details.cancel()` keeps it as it was.
    - `disabled?: boolean`: The trigger cannot be pressed; a submenu's is passed over.
    - `loop?: boolean`: Whether the arrows go round from the last item to the first. Default: they do.
    - `modal?: boolean`: Holds the page while the menu is open: its scroll is locked, and a press outside closes the menu and reaches nothing. Default: it does not. Not for a submenu.
- `<ContextMenu.SubmenuTrigger>` draws a `<div>`.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- trigger: The area a secondary press, or a long press on a touch screen, opens the menu in.
    - `data-popup-open`: Present when the menu is open.
- positioner: Places the menu against its trigger. It carries the geometry.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `--anchor-width`: The anchor's width.
    - `--anchor-height`: The anchor's height.
    - `--available-width`: The width between the anchor and the edge of the viewport.
    - `--available-height`: The height between the anchor and the edge of the viewport.
    - `--transform-origin`: The point of the popup nearest its anchor, to scale from.
- popup: The menu itself: the list of items.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
- arrow: An element that points at the trigger.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `data-uncentered`: Present when the arrow cannot sit at the trigger's centre.
- item: An action. Choosing it closes the menu.
    - `data-highlighted`: Present on the item the pointer or the keyboard is on.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- linkItem: An item that is a link. Choosing it follows the link and closes the menu.
    - `data-highlighted`: Present on the item the pointer or the keyboard is on.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- checkboxItem: An item that is checked or not. Choosing it leaves the menu open.
    - `data-checked`: Present when it is checked.
    - `data-unchecked`: Present when it is not checked.
    - `data-highlighted`: Present on the item the pointer or the keyboard is on.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- checkboxItemIndicator: A mark a checkbox item shows while it is checked.
    - `data-checked`: Present when it is checked.
    - `data-unchecked`: Present when it is not checked.
- radioGroup: Radio items of which one is chosen.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- radioItem: One choice of a radio group. Choosing it leaves the menu open.
    - `data-checked`: Present when it is checked.
    - `data-unchecked`: Present when it is not checked.
    - `data-highlighted`: Present on the item the pointer or the keyboard is on.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- radioItemIndicator: A mark a radio item shows while it is the chosen one.
    - `data-checked`: Present when it is checked.
    - `data-unchecked`: Present when it is not checked.
- submenuTrigger: An item that opens a menu beside it.
    - `data-popup-open`: Present when its menu is open.
    - `data-highlighted`: Present on the item the pointer or the keyboard is on.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.

### DateField

```
import { DateField } from "@kirana-ui/react/date-field"
```

Parts: `<DateField.Root>`, `<DateField.Segments>`, `<DateField.Segment>`, `<DateField.Input>`.

Anatomy:

```
<DateField.Root>
  <DateField.Segments>
    <DateField.Segment> (repeated)
  <DateField.Input>
```

Props of its root:

- `value?: IsoDate | null`: The day typed, once all of it is; `null` until then.
- `defaultValue?: IsoDate | null`: The value it starts with, when the caller does not hold `value`. Read once.
- `onValueChange?: (value: IsoDate | null, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Heard as the day is about to change, once all of it is typed or as it is cleared: `details.cancel()` keeps the value as it was.
- `locale?: string`: The language and region that order the day, the month and the year and put what stands between them (`"en-US"`: month/day/year). Give it: a server does not know the reader's. Default `"en-US"`.
- `min?: IsoDate`: The first and the last day it takes: outside them it says it is invalid.
- `max?: IsoDate`: The last day it takes.
- `placeholders?: Partial<Record<DateUnit, string>>`: What an empty part shows. Default: `dd`, `mm`, `yyyy`.
- `disabled?: boolean`: Disabled: it cannot be changed.
- `readOnly?: boolean`: Shown as it is, focusable, not changeable.
- `required?: boolean`: Needed: in a `Field`, leaving it empty is then invalid.
- `name?: string`: The name it is submitted under, by its hidden input.
- `form?: string`: The id of the form it belongs to, when it is not inside it.

Each part, and its own props:

- `<DateField.Root>` draws a `<div>`. Its props are above.
- `<DateField.Segments>` draws no element. The date's segments, in the locale's order: each is given to draw.
    - `children: (segment: DateFieldSegment) => ReactNode`: Required. Draws one piece of the date, once for each: a part that is typed, or what stands between two.
- `<DateField.Segment>` draws a `<span>`.
    - `segment: DateFieldSegment`: Required. The piece it is: an entry `DateField.Segments` gave.
- `<DateField.Input>` draws a `<input>`. The hidden input it is submitted by.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: The field: a group of the date's parts.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when its value cannot be changed.
    - `data-invalid`: Present when the date is outside what it takes, or is asked for and half typed.
- segment: One piece of the date: a part that is typed, or what stands between two.
    - `data-segment="day | month | year | literal"`: Which piece it is.
    - `data-placeholder`: Present on a part that is empty.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-invalid`: Present when the date is outside what it takes, or is asked for and half typed.

### DatePicker

```
import { DatePicker } from "@kirana-ui/react/date-picker"
```

Parts: `<DatePicker.Root>`, `<DatePicker.Field>`, `<DatePicker.Segments>`, `<DatePicker.Segment>`, `<DatePicker.Input>`, `<DatePicker.Trigger>`, `<DatePicker.Portal>`, `<DatePicker.Positioner>`, `<DatePicker.Popup>`, `<DatePicker.Calendar>`, `<DatePicker.Heading>`, `<DatePicker.Previous>`, `<DatePicker.Next>`, `<DatePicker.Months>`, `<DatePicker.Grid>`, `<DatePicker.Weekdays>`, `<DatePicker.HeadCell>`, `<DatePicker.Weeks>`, `<DatePicker.Cell>`, `<DatePicker.Day>`.

Anatomy:

```
<DatePicker.Root>
  <DatePicker.Field>
    <DatePicker.Segments>
      <DatePicker.Segment> (repeated)
    <DatePicker.Input>
  <DatePicker.Trigger>
  <DatePicker.Portal>
    <DatePicker.Positioner>
      <DatePicker.Popup>
        <DatePicker.Calendar>
          <DatePicker.Months> (optional)
            <DatePicker.Heading>
            <DatePicker.Grid>
              <DatePicker.Weekdays>
                <DatePicker.HeadCell> (repeated)
              <DatePicker.Weeks>
                <DatePicker.Cell> (repeated)
                  <DatePicker.Day>
          <DatePicker.Previous>
          <DatePicker.Next>
```

Props of its root:

- `value?: IsoDate | null`: The day, typed or picked; `null` for none.
- `defaultValue?: IsoDate | null`: The value it starts with, when the caller does not hold `value`. Read once.
- `onValueChange?: (value: IsoDate | null, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Heard as the day is about to change, typed or picked: `details.cancel()` keeps the value as it was.
- `open?: boolean`: Whether the calendar is open, when the caller holds it.
- `defaultOpen?: boolean`: Whether the calendar starts open, when the caller does not hold `open`. Read once.
- `onOpenChange?: (open: boolean, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Heard as the calendar is about to open or close: `details.cancel()` keeps it as it was.
- `locale?: string`: The language and region of the field and the calendar. Give it: a server does not know.
- `min?: IsoDate`: The first and the last day that can be typed or picked.
- `max?: IsoDate`: The last day that can be typed or picked.
- `isDateUnavailable?: (date: IsoDate) => boolean`: Days that cannot be picked in the calendar.
- `calendarSystem?: CalendarSystem`: The calendar its months are laid out in, when it is not the Gregorian one.
- `fixedWeeks?: boolean`: Always six rows of days.
- `months?: number`: How many months the calendar shows side by side (1 by default).
- `pagedNavigation?: boolean`: With several `months`: whether Previous and Next turn them all rather than one month.
- `month?: IsoDate`: The month the calendar shows (the first, with several), when the caller holds it.
- `defaultMonth?: IsoDate`: The month the calendar starts on, when the caller does not hold `month`. Read once.
- `onMonthChange?: (month: IsoDate, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Heard as the calendar is about to show another month, a day typed or picked included: its first day. `details.cancel()` keeps the month as it was.
- `placeholders?: Partial<Record<DateUnit, string>>`: What an empty part of the field shows.
- `disabled?: boolean`: Disabled: it cannot be changed.
- `readOnly?: boolean`: Shown as it is, focusable, not changeable.
- `required?: boolean`: Needed: in a `Field`, leaving it empty is then invalid.
- `name?: string`: The name it is submitted under.
- `form?: string`: The id of the form it belongs to, when it is not inside it.

Each part, and its own props:

- `<DatePicker.Root>` draws no element. Holds the date picker: its value, the month shown and whether the calendar is open. Its props are above.
- `<DatePicker.Field>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<DatePicker.Segments>` draws no element. The date's segments, in the locale's order: each is given to draw.
    - `children: (segment: DateFieldSegment) => ReactNode`: Required. Draws one piece of the date, once for each: a part that is typed, or what stands between two.
- `<DatePicker.Segment>` draws a `<span>`.
    - `segment: DateFieldSegment`: Required. The piece it is: an entry `DateField.Segments` gave.
- `<DatePicker.Input>` draws a `<input>`. The hidden input it is submitted by.
- `<DatePicker.Trigger>` draws a `<button>`.
    - `openOnHover?: boolean`: Whether the pointer resting on the trigger opens the popover too. A press and the keyboard still open it, and a press on one the pointer opened keeps it open. Default `false`.
    - `delay?: number`: How long the pointer rests on the trigger before the popover opens, in milliseconds. Default 300.
    - `closeDelay?: number`: How long after the pointer leaves a popover it opened closes, in milliseconds. Default 0.
- `<DatePicker.Portal>` draws no element. Draws no element of its own: its children at the end of `<body>`, or where a `PortalProvider` says.
- `<DatePicker.Positioner>` draws a `<div>`. Takes the positioner options ("Positioner options", above).
- `<DatePicker.Popup>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<DatePicker.Calendar>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<DatePicker.Heading>` draws a `<div>`. Names the month shown. Read out when it changes.
- `<DatePicker.Previous>` draws a `<button>`.
- `<DatePicker.Next>` draws a `<button>`.
- `<DatePicker.Months>` draws no element. The months shown, with several: each is given to draw its heading and its grid. It draws no element, and is left out for one month.
    - `children: (month: CalendarMonth) => ReactNode`: Required. Draws one month, once for each shown: its heading and its grid.
- `<DatePicker.Grid>` draws a `<table>`. The table of a month's days: a grid the arrows move in, from one month shown into the next.
- `<DatePicker.Weekdays>` draws no element. The days of the week: each is given to draw its head cell.
    - `children: (weekday: CalendarWeekday) => ReactNode`: Required. Draws one day of the week, once for each: its heading cell.
- `<DatePicker.HeadCell>` draws a `<th>`. A column's heading: a day of the week.
    - `weekday: CalendarWeekday`: Required. The day of the week it heads: an entry `Calendar.Weekdays` gave.
- `<DatePicker.Weeks>` draws no element. The weeks of the month shown: each is given to draw its row of days.
    - `children: (week: readonly CalendarDay[]) => ReactNode`: Required. Draws one week, once for each of the month shown: a row of its days.
- `<DatePicker.Cell>` draws a `<td>`.
    - `date: string`: Required. The day it holds, as `Calendar.Weeks` gave it: `day.date`.
- `<DatePicker.Day>` draws a `<button>`.
    - `date: string`: Required. The day it is the button of, as `Calendar.Weeks` gave it: `day.date`.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- field: The field: a group of the date's parts.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when its value cannot be changed.
    - `data-invalid`: Present when the date is outside what it takes, or is asked for and half typed.
- segment: One piece of the date: a part that is typed, or what stands between two.
    - `data-segment="day | month | year | literal"`: Which piece it is.
    - `data-placeholder`: Present on a part that is empty.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-invalid`: Present when the date is outside what it takes, or is asked for and half typed.
- trigger: The button that opens the popover, and what it is placed against.
    - `data-popup-open`: Present when the popover is open.
- positioner: Places the popup against the trigger. It carries the geometry.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `--anchor-width`: The anchor's width.
    - `--anchor-height`: The anchor's height.
    - `--available-width`: The width between the anchor and the edge of the viewport.
    - `--available-height`: The height between the anchor and the edge of the viewport.
    - `--transform-origin`: The point of the popup nearest its anchor, to scale from.
- popup: The popover itself.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
- calendar: The calendar.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when its value cannot be changed.
- previous: Shows the month before.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- next: Shows the month after.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- cell: A day's cell.
    - `data-selected`: Present on a chosen day, on every day of a chosen range, and on each day of a list. Never on a copy: a day of the month before or after shown in its own month too.
    - `data-today`: Present on today.
    - `data-outside-month`: Present on the days of the month before and after that fill the first and last weeks.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-unavailable`: Present on a day that cannot be chosen.
    - `data-range-start`: Present on the first day of a range.
    - `data-range-end`: Present on the last day of a range.
- day: The button for a day.
    - `data-selected`: Present on a chosen day, on every day of a chosen range, and on each day of a list. Never on a copy: a day of the month before or after shown in its own month too.
    - `data-today`: Present on today.
    - `data-outside-month`: Present on the days of the month before and after that fill the first and last weeks.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-unavailable`: Present on a day that cannot be chosen.
    - `data-range-start`: Present on the first day of a range.
    - `data-range-end`: Present on the last day of a range.

### Dialog

```
import { Dialog } from "@kirana-ui/react/dialog"
```

Parts: `<Dialog.Root>`, `<Dialog.Trigger>`, `<Dialog.Portal>`, `<Dialog.Backdrop>`, `<Dialog.Viewport>`, `<Dialog.Popup>`, `<Dialog.Title>`, `<Dialog.Description>`, `<Dialog.Close>`.

Anatomy:

```
<Dialog.Root>
  <Dialog.Trigger>
  <Dialog.Portal>
    <Dialog.Backdrop>
    <Dialog.Viewport> (optional)
      <Dialog.Popup>
        <Dialog.Title>
        <Dialog.Description>
        <Dialog.Close>
```

Props of its root:

- `open?: boolean`: Whether it is open, when the caller holds it.
- `defaultOpen?: boolean`: Whether it starts open, when the caller does not hold `open`. Read once.
- `onOpenChange?: (open: boolean, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Heard as it is about to open or close: `details.cancel()` keeps it as it was.
- `modal?: boolean`: Blocks the page behind it and traps focus. Default `true`.
- `dismissible?: boolean`: Whether a press outside closes it. Default `true`.

Each part, and its own props:

- `<Dialog.Root>` draws no element. Holds the dialog: whether it is open. Its props are above.
- `<Dialog.Trigger>` draws a `<button>`.
- `<Dialog.Portal>` draws no element. Draws no element of its own: its children at the end of `<body>`, or where a `PortalProvider` says.
- `<Dialog.Backdrop>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<Dialog.Viewport>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<Dialog.Popup>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<Dialog.Title>` draws a `<h2>`. The heading that names the dialog.
- `<Dialog.Description>` draws a `<p>`. The text that describes the dialog.
- `<Dialog.Close>` draws a `<button>`. A button that closes the dialog.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- trigger: The button that opens the dialog.
    - `data-popup-open`: Present when the dialog is open.
- backdrop: The layer over the page behind the dialog.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
- viewport: What a long dialog scrolls in: it lies over the page, between the backdrop and the popup. A press on it beside the popup is a press outside the dialog; a press on its scrollbar is not.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
    - `data-nested`: Present when the dialog opened over another dialog.
    - `data-nested-dialog-open`: Present when another dialog is open above this one.
- popup: The dialog itself.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
    - `data-nested-dialog-open`: Present when another dialog is open above this one.
    - `--nested-dialogs`: How many dialogs are open above this one.

### Drawer

```
import { Drawer } from "@kirana-ui/react/drawer"
```

Parts: `<Drawer.Root>`, `<Drawer.Trigger>`, `<Drawer.Portal>`, `<Drawer.Backdrop>`, `<Drawer.Popup>`, `<Drawer.Title>`, `<Drawer.Description>`, `<Drawer.Close>`.

Anatomy:

```
<Drawer.Root>
  <Drawer.Trigger>
  <Drawer.Portal>
    <Drawer.Backdrop>
    <Drawer.Popup>
      <Drawer.Title>
      <Drawer.Description>
      <Drawer.Close>
```

Props of its root:

- `open?: boolean`: Whether it is open, when the caller holds it.
- `defaultOpen?: boolean`: Whether it starts open, when the caller does not hold `open`. Read once.
- `onOpenChange?: (open: boolean, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Heard as it is about to open or close: `details.cancel()` keeps it as it was.
- `modal?: boolean`: Blocks the page behind it and traps focus. Default `true`.
- `dismissible?: boolean`: Whether a press outside closes it. Default `true`.
- `swipeDirection?: DrawerSide`: The way it is dragged to close it: the edge it came from. Default: `"down"`.
- `snapPoints?: readonly DrawerSnapPoint[]`: Places it rests at, each how much of itself shows: a share (`0.4`, or `"40%"`) or a length (`"148px"`, `"20rem"`). `[0.4, 1]` is a drawer that opens two fifths shown and is dragged up to the whole. Without any, it is whole.
- `snapPoint?: DrawerSnapPoint`: Which of them it rests at, as it was given.
- `defaultSnapPoint?: DrawerSnapPoint`: Where it opens. Default: the smallest.
- `onSnapPointChange?: (snapPoint: DrawerSnapPoint, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Heard as it is about to rest at another snap point: `details.cancel()` keeps it where it was.

Each part, and its own props:

- `<Drawer.Root>` draws no element. Holds the dialog: whether it is open. Its props are above.
- `<Drawer.Trigger>` draws a `<button>`.
- `<Drawer.Portal>` draws no element. Draws no element of its own: its children at the end of `<body>`, or where a `PortalProvider` says.
- `<Drawer.Backdrop>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<Drawer.Popup>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<Drawer.Title>` draws a `<h2>`. The heading that names the dialog.
- `<Drawer.Description>` draws a `<p>`. The text that describes the dialog.
- `<Drawer.Close>` draws a `<button>`. A button that closes the dialog.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- trigger: The button that opens the dialog.
    - `data-popup-open`: Present when the dialog is open.
- backdrop: The layer over the page behind the dialog.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
    - `data-swiping`: Present while the drawer is dragged.
    - `--drawer-swipe-movement-x`: How far it has been dragged across.
    - `--drawer-swipe-movement-y`: How far it has been dragged up or down.
    - `--drawer-swipe-progress`: How far it has been dragged, of its own size: 0 to 1.
    - `--drawer-snap-point-offset`: How far from whole it rests, towards the edge it closes at: 0px at its largest snap point.
- popup: The drawer. A design moves it by what it says of the drag, and gives it `touch-action: none` where a finger drags it.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
    - `data-nested-dialog-open`: Present when another dialog is open above this one.
    - `data-swiping`: Present while the drawer is dragged.
    - `data-swipe-direction="up | down | left | right"`: The way it is dragged to close it.
    - `data-swipe-dismiss`: Present once a drag has closed it.
    - `data-expanded`: Present while it rests whole, of several snap points.
    - `data-nested-drawer-open`: Present while another drawer is open over it.
    - `data-nested-drawer-swiping`: Present while a drawer over it is dragged.
    - `--nested-dialogs`: How many dialogs are open above this one.
    - `--drawer-swipe-movement-x`: How far it has been dragged across.
    - `--drawer-swipe-movement-y`: How far it has been dragged up or down.
    - `--drawer-swipe-progress`: How far it has been dragged, of its own size: 0 to 1.
    - `--drawer-snap-point-offset`: How far from whole it rests, towards the edge it closes at: 0px at its largest snap point.
    - `--drawer-height`: Its height.
    - `--nested-drawers`: How many drawers are open over it.
    - `--drawer-frontmost-height`: The height of the drawer in front of every other, while this one is open.
    - `--drawer-swipe-strength`: Once let go: 0.1 to 1, the share of the design's own time it should take to come to rest. A drawer thrown hard arrives sooner.
    - `--drawer-width`: Its width.

### Field

```
import { Field } from "@kirana-ui/react/field"
```

Parts: `<Field.Root>`, `<Field.Label>`, `<Field.Control>`, `<Field.Description>`, `<Field.Error>`, `<Field.Validity>`.

Anatomy:

```
<Field.Root>
  <Field.Label>
  <Field.Control>
  <Field.Description>
  <Field.Error>
  <Field.Validity>
```

Props of its root:

- `name?: string`: The control's name in the form.
- `disabled?: boolean`: Disables the field: its control cannot be changed, and its parts say so (`data-disabled`).
- `invalid?: boolean`: Invalid whatever the value: an error known from elsewhere.
- `validate?: ( value: string ) => string | readonly string[] | null | Promise<string | readonly string[] | null>`: The field's own check, after the browser's: a message or several when the value is wrong, `null` when it is right. It may answer later, with a promise.
- `validationMode?: ValidationMode`: When the value is checked; the form's by default, else `"onSubmit"`.
- `validationDebounceTime?: number`: With `"onChange"`, how long the value must rest before it is checked, in milliseconds. Default `0`.

Each part, and its own props:

- `<Field.Root>` draws a `<div>`. Its props are above.
- `<Field.Label>` draws a `<label>`.
- `<Field.Control>` draws a `<input>`.
- `<Field.Description>` draws a `<p>`.
- `<Field.Error>` draws a `<div>`.
    - `match?: ValidityKey | boolean`: One of the browser's findings (`"valueMissing"`) to show for only that; `true` to show always.
- `<Field.Validity>` draws no element. Gives the control's validity to what it holds, to draw from.
    - `children: (validity: FieldValidity) => ReactNode`: Required. Draws from the field's validity: whether it is valid, what was found wrong, the messages.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: A control with its label, its description and its errors.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-touched`: Present once focus has left the control.
    - `data-dirty`: Present while the value is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Present while the control has a value.
    - `data-focused`: Present while the control has focus.
    - `data-valid`: Present once the value has been checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: Present while the value is wrong.
- label: The control's name: a press on it reaches the control.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-touched`: Present once focus has left the control.
    - `data-dirty`: Present while the value is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Present while the control has a value.
    - `data-focused`: Present while the control has focus.
    - `data-valid`: Present once the value has been checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: Present while the value is wrong.
- control: The control: an input, a textarea or a select.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-touched`: Present once focus has left the control.
    - `data-dirty`: Present while the value is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Present while the control has a value.
    - `data-focused`: Present while the control has focus.
    - `data-valid`: Present once the value has been checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: Present while the value is wrong.
- description: More about the control, said after its name.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-touched`: Present once focus has left the control.
    - `data-dirty`: Present while the value is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Present while the control has a value.
    - `data-focused`: Present while the control has focus.
    - `data-valid`: Present once the value has been checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: Present while the value is wrong.
- error: What is wrong with the value. In the page while it applies.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-touched`: Present once focus has left the control.
    - `data-dirty`: Present while the value is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Present while the control has a value.
    - `data-focused`: Present while the control has focus.
    - `data-valid`: Present once the value has been checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: Present while the value is wrong.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.

### Fieldset

```
import { Fieldset } from "@kirana-ui/react/fieldset"
```

Parts: `<Fieldset.Root>`, `<Fieldset.Legend>`.

Anatomy:

```
<Fieldset.Root>
  <Fieldset.Legend>
```

Props of its root:

- `disabled?: boolean`: Disables every field inside.

Each part, and its own props:

- `<Fieldset.Root>` draws a `<fieldset>`. Its props are above.
- `<Fieldset.Legend>` draws a `<div>`.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: The group of fields.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- legend: The group's name.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.

### Form

```
import { Form } from "@kirana-ui/react/form"
```

Props:

- `errors?: FormErrors`: Errors from outside the page (a server's), by field name. A field shows its own until its value changes.
- `onClearErrors?: (errors: FormErrors) => void`: A field's value changed while it showed an error from `errors`: what is left of them.
- `onFormSubmit?: (values: FormValues, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Every field is valid. Given this, the page is not left: the values come as an object. Without it, the form submits as a form does.
- `validationMode?: ValidationMode`: When the form's fields check their values, unless a field says otherwise. Default `"onSubmit"`.

`<Form>` draws a `<form>`. The form. A submit checks every field in it and stops, with focus on the first that is invalid.

### HoverCard

```
import { HoverCard } from "@kirana-ui/react/hover-card"
```

Parts: `<HoverCard.Root>`, `<HoverCard.Trigger>`, `<HoverCard.Portal>`, `<HoverCard.Positioner>`, `<HoverCard.Popup>`, `<HoverCard.Arrow>`.

Anatomy:

```
<HoverCard.Root>
  <HoverCard.Trigger>
  <HoverCard.Portal>
    <HoverCard.Positioner>
      <HoverCard.Popup>
        <HoverCard.Arrow>
```

Props of its root:

- `open?: boolean`: Whether it is open, when the caller holds it.
- `defaultOpen?: boolean`: Whether it starts open, when the caller does not hold `open`. Read once.
- `onOpenChange?: (open: boolean, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Heard as it is about to open or close: `details.cancel()` keeps it as it was.
- `delay?: number`: How long the pointer rests on the trigger before the popup opens, in milliseconds. Default `600`.
- `closeDelay?: number`: How long after the pointer leaves the popup closes, in milliseconds. Default `300`.
- `disabled?: boolean`: Disabled: the pointer and focus do not open it.

Each part, and its own props:

- `<HoverCard.Root>` draws no element. Holds the card: whether it is open. Its props are above.
- `<HoverCard.Trigger>` draws a `<a>`.
    - `delay?: number`: How long the pointer rests on this trigger before the popup opens, in milliseconds.
    - `closeDelay?: number`: How long after the pointer leaves this trigger's popup closes, in milliseconds.
- `<HoverCard.Portal>` draws no element. Draws no element of its own: its children at the end of `<body>`, or where a `PortalProvider` says.
- `<HoverCard.Positioner>` draws a `<div>`. Takes the positioner options ("Positioner options", above).
- `<HoverCard.Popup>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<HoverCard.Arrow>` draws a `<div>`.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- trigger: The link the card previews.
    - `data-popup-open`: Present when the card is open.
- positioner: Places the popup against the trigger. It carries the geometry.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `--anchor-width`: The anchor's width.
    - `--anchor-height`: The anchor's height.
    - `--available-width`: The width between the anchor and the edge of the viewport.
    - `--available-height`: The height between the anchor and the edge of the viewport.
    - `--transform-origin`: The point of the popup nearest its anchor, to scale from.
- popup: The card itself.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `data-instant="delay | focus | dismiss"`: Present when it opened or closed without its usual wait, for a design that skips the motion then.
- arrow: An element that points at the trigger, placed along the popup's edge.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `data-uncentered`: Present when the popup was pushed along its edge, so the arrow is not at the trigger's centre.

### Input

```
import { Input } from "@kirana-ui/react/input"
```

Props:

- `disabled?: boolean`: Disabled: nothing can be typed in it.
- `onValueChange?: (value: string, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: What was typed, as text, each time it changes.

`<Input>` draws a `<input>`.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- input: A text input. Inside a field it is the field's control.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-touched`: Present once focus has left the input.
    - `data-dirty`: Present while the value is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Present while the input has a value.
    - `data-focused`: Present while the input has focus.
    - `data-valid`: In a field: present once the value was checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: In a field: present while the value is wrong.

### Label

```
import { Label } from "@kirana-ui/react/label"
```

`<Label>` draws a `<label>`.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- label: A control's name. Inside a field it is the field's label, with its states.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-touched`: Present once focus has left the control.
    - `data-dirty`: Present while the value is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Present while the control has a value.
    - `data-focused`: Present while the control has focus.
    - `data-valid`: Present once the value has been checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: Present while the value is wrong.

### Listbox

```
import { Listbox } from "@kirana-ui/react/listbox"
```

Parts: `<Listbox.Root>`, `<Listbox.Item>`, `<Listbox.ItemIndicator>`, `<Listbox.Group>`, `<Listbox.GroupLabel>`.

Anatomy:

```
<Listbox.Root>
  <Listbox.Group> (optional, repeated)
    <Listbox.Item> (repeated)
      <Listbox.ItemIndicator>
    <Listbox.GroupLabel>
```

Props of its root:

- `value?: readonly Value[]`: The chosen values: none, one, or with `multiple` several.
- `defaultValue?: readonly Value[]`: The values it starts with, when the caller does not hold `value`. Read once.
- `onValueChange?: (value: Value[], details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Heard as an item is about to be chosen or taken away, with the values there would then be: `details.cancel()` keeps them as they were.
- `multiple?: boolean`: Whether more than one can be chosen: a press then adds or takes away.
- `disabled?: boolean`: Disabled: no item can be chosen.
- `loop?: boolean`: Whether the arrows go round from the last item to the first. Default: they do not.
- `name?: string`: With a name, the chosen values are submitted with the form around the list.
- `form?: string`: The id of the form the list belongs to, when it is not inside it.
- `virtualized?: ListCollection`: Every row, when only some are in the page (a virtualizer draws the ones in view): how many there are, their names, and how to bring one into the page. Each item is then given its `index`.

Each part, and its own props:

- `<Listbox.Root>` draws a `<div>`. Generic: `<Value = unknown>`. `Value` is what tells an item from the others: the type of `value`'s entries. Its props are above.
- `<Listbox.Item>` draws a `<div>`.
    - `disabled?: boolean`: Disables this item: it cannot be chosen, and the arrows pass over it.
    - `label?: string`: What typing matches; the item's text when left out.
    - `index?: number`: Its place among all the rows, in a virtualized list.
    - `value: unknown`: Required. What is in the listbox's value while this item is chosen.
- `<Listbox.ItemIndicator>` draws a `<span>`.
    - `keepMounted?: boolean`: Keeps the mark in the page while its item is not chosen.
- `<Listbox.Group>` draws a `<div>`. Items that belong together, named by their label.
- `<Listbox.GroupLabel>` draws a `<div>`. The name of a group.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: The list. It is one stop for Tab.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- item: One choice in the list.
    - `data-selected`: Present on a chosen item.
    - `data-highlighted`: Present on the item the keyboard is on.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- itemIndicator: A mark an item shows while it is chosen.
    - `data-selected`: Present on a chosen item.

### Menu

```
import { Menu } from "@kirana-ui/react/menu"
```

Parts: `<Menu.Root>`, `<Menu.Trigger>`, `<Menu.Portal>`, `<Menu.Positioner>`, `<Menu.Popup>`, `<Menu.Arrow>`, `<Menu.Item>`, `<Menu.LinkItem>`, `<Menu.Group>`, `<Menu.GroupLabel>`, `<Menu.Separator>`, `<Menu.CheckboxItem>`, `<Menu.CheckboxItemIndicator>`, `<Menu.RadioGroup>`, `<Menu.RadioItem>`, `<Menu.RadioItemIndicator>`, `<Menu.SubmenuRoot>`, `<Menu.SubmenuTrigger>`.

Anatomy:

```
<Menu.Root>
  <Menu.Trigger>
  <Menu.Portal>
    <Menu.Positioner>
      <Menu.Popup>
        <Menu.Arrow>
        <Menu.Group> (optional, repeated)
          <Menu.Item> (repeated)
          <Menu.LinkItem> (repeated)
          <Menu.GroupLabel>
          <Menu.CheckboxItem> (repeated)
            <Menu.CheckboxItemIndicator>
          <Menu.RadioGroup> (repeated)
            <Menu.RadioItem> (repeated)
              <Menu.RadioItemIndicator>
          <Menu.SubmenuRoot> (repeated)
            <Menu.Portal> (as above)
            <Menu.SubmenuTrigger>
        <Menu.Separator> (repeated)
```

Props of its root:

- `open?: boolean`: Whether it is open, when the caller holds it.
- `defaultOpen?: boolean`: Whether it starts open, when the caller does not hold `open`. Read once.
- `onOpenChange?: (open: boolean, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Heard as it is about to open or close: `details.cancel()` keeps it as it was.
- `disabled?: boolean`: The trigger cannot be pressed; a submenu's is passed over.
- `loop?: boolean`: Whether the arrows go round from the last item to the first. Default: they do.
- `modal?: boolean`: Holds the page while the menu is open: its scroll is locked, and a press outside closes the menu and reaches nothing. Default: it does not. Not for a submenu.

Each part, and its own props:

- `<Menu.Root>` draws no element. Holds the menu: whether it is open. Its props are above.
- `<Menu.Trigger>` draws a `<button>`.
- `<Menu.Portal>` draws no element. Draws no element of its own: its children at the end of `<body>`, or where a `PortalProvider` says.
- `<Menu.Positioner>` draws a `<div>`. Takes the positioner options ("Positioner options", above).
- `<Menu.Popup>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<Menu.Arrow>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<Menu.Item>` draws a `<div>`.
    - `disabled?: boolean`: Disables this item: it cannot be pressed, and the arrows pass over it.
    - `label?: string`: What typing matches; the item's text when left out.
    - `closeOnClick?: boolean`: Whether choosing the item closes the menu. Default: it does for an item, and does not for a checkbox or a radio item.
- `<Menu.LinkItem>` draws a `<a>`.
    - `disabled?: boolean`: Disables this item: it cannot be pressed, and the arrows pass over it.
    - `label?: string`: What typing matches; the item's text when left out.
    - `closeOnClick?: boolean`: Whether choosing the item closes the menu. Default: it does for an item, and does not for a checkbox or a radio item.
- `<Menu.Group>` draws a `<div>`. Items that belong together, named by their label.
- `<Menu.GroupLabel>` draws a `<div>`. The name of a group. Outside a group it is plain text, and names nothing.
- `<Menu.Separator>` draws a `<div>`. A line between items.
- `<Menu.CheckboxItem>` draws a `<div>`.
    - `disabled?: boolean`: Disables this item: it cannot be pressed, and the arrows pass over it.
    - `label?: string`: What typing matches; the item's text when left out.
    - `closeOnClick?: boolean`: Whether choosing the item closes the menu. Default: it does for an item, and does not for a checkbox or a radio item.
    - `checked?: boolean`: Whether the item is checked, when the caller holds it.
    - `defaultChecked?: boolean`: Whether the item starts checked, when the caller does not hold `checked`. Read once.
    - `onCheckedChange?: (checked: boolean, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Heard as the item is about to be checked or unchecked: `details.cancel()` keeps it as it was.
- `<Menu.CheckboxItemIndicator>` draws a `<span>`.
    - `keepMounted?: boolean`: Keeps the mark in the page while its item is not checked.
- `<Menu.RadioGroup>` draws a `<div>`. Generic: `<Value = unknown>`. `Value` is what tells a radio item from the others: the type of `value`.
    - `value?: Value | null`: The chosen value; `null` is "none".
    - `defaultValue?: Value | null`: The value it starts with, when the caller does not hold `value`. Read once.
    - `onValueChange?: (value: Value, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Told an item's own value, never `null`: a press chooses, and nothing takes the choice back.
    - `disabled?: boolean`: Disables every item of the group.
- `<Menu.RadioItem>` draws a `<div>`.
    - `disabled?: boolean`: Disables this item: it cannot be pressed, and the arrows pass over it.
    - `label?: string`: What typing matches; the item's text when left out.
    - `closeOnClick?: boolean`: Whether choosing the item closes the menu. Default: it does for an item, and does not for a checkbox or a radio item.
    - `value: unknown`: Required. What the radio group's value is while this item is the chosen one.
- `<Menu.RadioItemIndicator>` draws a `<span>`.
    - `keepMounted?: boolean`: Keeps the mark in the page while its item is not checked.
- `<Menu.SubmenuRoot>` draws no element. A submenu: it holds the item that opens it and a portal, positioner and popup of its own.
    - `open?: boolean`: Whether it is open, when the caller holds it.
    - `defaultOpen?: boolean`: Whether it starts open, when the caller does not hold `open`. Read once.
    - `onOpenChange?: (open: boolean, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Heard as it is about to open or close: `details.cancel()` keeps it as it was.
    - `disabled?: boolean`: The trigger cannot be pressed; a submenu's is passed over.
    - `loop?: boolean`: Whether the arrows go round from the last item to the first. Default: they do.
    - `modal?: boolean`: Holds the page while the menu is open: its scroll is locked, and a press outside closes the menu and reaches nothing. Default: it does not. Not for a submenu.
- `<Menu.SubmenuTrigger>` draws a `<div>`.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- trigger: The button that opens the menu, and what it is placed against.
    - `data-popup-open`: Present when the menu is open.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- positioner: Places the menu against its trigger. It carries the geometry.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `--anchor-width`: The anchor's width.
    - `--anchor-height`: The anchor's height.
    - `--available-width`: The width between the anchor and the edge of the viewport.
    - `--available-height`: The height between the anchor and the edge of the viewport.
    - `--transform-origin`: The point of the popup nearest its anchor, to scale from.
- popup: The menu itself: the list of items.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
- arrow: An element that points at the trigger.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `data-uncentered`: Present when the arrow cannot sit at the trigger's centre.
- item: An action. Choosing it closes the menu.
    - `data-highlighted`: Present on the item the pointer or the keyboard is on.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- linkItem: An item that is a link. Choosing it follows the link and closes the menu.
    - `data-highlighted`: Present on the item the pointer or the keyboard is on.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- checkboxItem: An item that is checked or not. Choosing it leaves the menu open.
    - `data-checked`: Present when it is checked.
    - `data-unchecked`: Present when it is not checked.
    - `data-highlighted`: Present on the item the pointer or the keyboard is on.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- checkboxItemIndicator: A mark a checkbox item shows while it is checked.
    - `data-checked`: Present when it is checked.
    - `data-unchecked`: Present when it is not checked.
- radioGroup: Radio items of which one is chosen.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- radioItem: One choice of a radio group. Choosing it leaves the menu open.
    - `data-checked`: Present when it is checked.
    - `data-unchecked`: Present when it is not checked.
    - `data-highlighted`: Present on the item the pointer or the keyboard is on.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- radioItemIndicator: A mark a radio item shows while it is the chosen one.
    - `data-checked`: Present when it is checked.
    - `data-unchecked`: Present when it is not checked.
- submenuTrigger: An item that opens a menu beside it.
    - `data-popup-open`: Present when its menu is open.
    - `data-highlighted`: Present on the item the pointer or the keyboard is on.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.

### Menubar

```
import { Menubar } from "@kirana-ui/react/menubar"
```

Props:

- `loop?: boolean`: Whether the arrows go round from the last menu to the first. Default: they do.
- `disabled?: boolean`: No menu of the bar opens.
- `orientation?: Orientation`: A row (the default) or a column of menus. In a column a menu opens beside its trigger.

`<Menubar>` draws a `<div>`.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: The row of menus. A menu inside it is one of its items.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: Whether its menus are in a row or a column.

### MessageScroller

```
import { MessageScroller } from "@kirana-ui/react/message-scroller"
```

Parts: `<MessageScroller.Root>`, `<MessageScroller.Viewport>`, `<MessageScroller.Content>`, `<MessageScroller.Button>`.

Anatomy:

```
<MessageScroller.Root>
  <MessageScroller.Viewport>
    <MessageScroller.Content>
  <MessageScroller.Button>
```

Props of its root:

- `initial?: "bottom" | "top"`: Where it begins: at the newest message (the default), or at the first.
- `threshold?: number`: How near the end counts as at it, in pixels. Default: 24.
- `onAtBottomChange?: (atBottom: boolean, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Heard when it comes to the end or leaves it.

Each part, and its own props:

- `<MessageScroller.Root>` draws a `<div>`. Its props are above.
- `<MessageScroller.Viewport>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<MessageScroller.Content>` draws a `<div>`. The messages: what grows as one is written.
- `<MessageScroller.Button>` draws a `<button>`.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: What holds the conversation and its button.
    - `data-at-bottom`: Present while the newest message is in view.
- viewport: What scrolls: a log, reached by the keyboard.
    - `data-at-bottom`: Present while the newest message is in view.
