- button: Goes to the newest message. Inert while that is in view.
    - `data-at-bottom`: Present while the newest message is in view.

### Meter

```
import { Meter } from "@kirana-ui/react/meter"
```

Parts: `<Meter.Root>`, `<Meter.Track>`, `<Meter.Indicator>`, `<Meter.Value>`, `<Meter.Label>`.

Anatomy:

```
<Meter.Root>
  <Meter.Track>
    <Meter.Indicator>
  <Meter.Value>
  <Meter.Label>
```

Props of its root:

- `value: number`: Required. The measure, between `min` and `max`. A meter always has one.
- `min?: number`: Default 0.
- `max?: number`: Default 100.
- `format?: Intl.NumberFormatOptions`: How the value is written; a percentage of the range by default.
- `locale?: string`: The language the value is written in; the page's by default.
- `getAriaValueText?: (text: string | undefined, value: number | null) => string`: What assistive technology reads for the value, when the written value is not enough.

Each part, and its own props:

- `<Meter.Root>` draws a `<div>`. The meter: it says the value to assistive technology. Its props are above.
- `<Meter.Track>` draws a `<div>`. The whole range.
- `<Meter.Indicator>` draws a `<div>`. The filled part: its width is the value's share of the range.
- `<Meter.Value>` draws a `<span>`. The value, written.
    - `children?: (text: string | undefined) => ReactNode`: Draws something else than the written value: it is given the text, `undefined` while there is none.
- `<Meter.Label>` draws a `<span>`. The meter's name.

### NavigationMenu

```
import { NavigationMenu } from "@kirana-ui/react/navigation-menu"
```

Parts: `<NavigationMenu.Root>`, `<NavigationMenu.List>`, `<NavigationMenu.Item>`, `<NavigationMenu.Trigger>`, `<NavigationMenu.Icon>`, `<NavigationMenu.Content>`, `<NavigationMenu.Link>`, `<NavigationMenu.Portal>`, `<NavigationMenu.Positioner>`, `<NavigationMenu.Popup>`, `<NavigationMenu.Viewport>`, `<NavigationMenu.Arrow>`, `<NavigationMenu.Backdrop>`.

Anatomy:

```
<NavigationMenu.Root>
  <NavigationMenu.List>
    <NavigationMenu.Item> (repeated)
      <NavigationMenu.Trigger>
        <NavigationMenu.Icon>
      <NavigationMenu.Content>
        <NavigationMenu.Link> (repeated)
      <NavigationMenu.Link> (repeated, as above)
    <NavigationMenu.Link> (repeated, as above)
  <NavigationMenu.Portal>
    <NavigationMenu.Positioner>
      <NavigationMenu.Popup>
        <NavigationMenu.Viewport>
        <NavigationMenu.Arrow>
    <NavigationMenu.Backdrop>
```

Props of its root:

- `value?: Value | null`: The item whose content is shown; `null` is "none".
- `defaultValue?: Value | null`: The item whose content it starts with, when the caller does not hold `value`. Read once.
- `onValueChange?: (value: Value | null, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Heard as another item's content is about to show, or none: `details.cancel()` keeps the value as it was.
- `delay?: number`: How long the pointer rests on a trigger before its content shows, in milliseconds. Default `50`.
- `closeDelay?: number`: How long after the pointer leaves the content goes, in milliseconds. Default `50`.
- `orientation?: Orientation`: Whether the triggers are laid out across (the default) or down: the arrows that move between them follow.

Each part, and its own props:

- `<NavigationMenu.Root>` draws a `<nav>`. Generic: `<Value = unknown>`. `Value` is what tells an item from the others: the type of `value`. Its props are above.
- `<NavigationMenu.List>` draws a `<ul>`.
- `<NavigationMenu.Item>` draws a `<li>`. One item of the list: a link, or a trigger with its content. Its `value` tells it from the others; an item that is given none makes its own.
    - `value?: unknown`: What tells this item from the others: the menu's `value` while its content is shown. An item that is given none makes its own.
- `<NavigationMenu.Trigger>` draws a `<button>`.
- `<NavigationMenu.Icon>` draws a `<span>`.
- `<NavigationMenu.Content>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<NavigationMenu.Link>` draws a `<a>`.
    - `active?: boolean`: The link is the page the reader is on.
    - `closeOnClick?: boolean`: Whether following it closes the menu. Default: it does.
- `<NavigationMenu.Portal>` draws no element. Draws no element of its own: its children at the end of `<body>`, or where a `PortalProvider` says.
- `<NavigationMenu.Positioner>` draws a `<div>`. Takes the positioner options ("Positioner options", above).
- `<NavigationMenu.Popup>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<NavigationMenu.Viewport>` draws a `<div>`. Where the contents are drawn, inside the popup.
- `<NavigationMenu.Arrow>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<NavigationMenu.Backdrop>` draws a `<div>`.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: The navigation.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: Whether the list is a row or a column.
- list: The row of items.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: Whether the list is a row or a column.
- trigger: The button that shows an item's content.
    - `data-popup-open`: Present while the item's content is shown.
- icon: A mark on a trigger that shows whether its content is open.
    - `data-popup-open`: Present while the item's content is shown.
- content: What an item shows. It is drawn in the viewport every item shares.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
    - `data-activation-direction="left | right"`: Which way it came from: the item before it, or after.
- link: A link, in the list or in an item's content.
    - `data-active`: Present on the link of the page the reader is on.
- positioner: Places the popup against the open item's trigger. It carries the geometry.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `--anchor-width`: The anchor's width.
    - `--anchor-height`: The anchor's height.
    - `--available-width`: The width between the anchor and the edge of the viewport.
    - `--available-height`: The height between the anchor and the edge of the viewport.
    - `--transform-origin`: The point of the popup nearest its anchor, to scale from.
    - `--positioner-width`: The open content's width.
    - `--positioner-height`: The open content's height.
- popup: The panel every item's content is shown in.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `--popup-width`: The open content's width.
    - `--popup-height`: The open content's height.
- arrow: An element that points at the open item's trigger.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `data-uncentered`: Present when the arrow cannot sit at the trigger's centre.
- backdrop: An element behind the popup, for a design that dims the page.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.

### NumberField

```
import { NumberField } from "@kirana-ui/react/number-field"
```

Parts: `<NumberField.Root>`, `<NumberField.Group>`, `<NumberField.Input>`, `<NumberField.Increment>`, `<NumberField.Decrement>`, `<NumberField.ScrubArea>`, `<NumberField.ScrubAreaCursor>`.

Anatomy:

```
<NumberField.Root>
  <NumberField.Group>
    <NumberField.Input>
    <NumberField.Increment>
    <NumberField.Decrement>
  <NumberField.ScrubArea>
    <NumberField.ScrubAreaCursor>
```

Props of its root:

- `value?: number | null`: The number; `null` is "none".
- `defaultValue?: number | null`: The value it starts with, when the caller does not hold `value`. Read once.
- `onValueChange?: (value: number | null, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Heard as the number is about to change, typed or stepped: `details.cancel()` keeps it as it was.
- `onValueCommitted?: (value: number | null, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Heard once a change is done: focus left the input, a key or a button stepped it.
- `min?: number`: The least the number may be.
- `max?: number`: The most the number may be.
- `step?: number`: What the buttons and the arrows move by. Default 1.
- `smallStep?: number`: With Alt held. Default 0.1.
- `largeStep?: number`: With Shift held. Default 10.
- `snapOnStep?: boolean`: A step lands on a multiple of the step, counted from `min`.
- `allowWheelScrub?: boolean`: The wheel steps it while the pointer is over the input and focus is in it.
- `format?: Intl.NumberFormatOptions`: How the number is written.
- `locale?: string`: The language it is written in; the page's by default.
- `disabled?: boolean`: Disabled: it cannot be changed.
- `readOnly?: boolean`: Shown as it is, focusable, not changeable.
- `required?: boolean`: Needed: in a `Field`, leaving it empty is then invalid.
- `name?: string`: With a name, the number is submitted with the form around it.
- `form?: string`: The id of the form the control belongs to, when it is not inside it.
- `id?: string`: What its input's id is made from: the input is `<id>-input`, which a `<label for>` names. Inside a `Field`, the input takes the field's id instead.

Each part, and its own props:

- `<NumberField.Root>` draws a `<div>`. Its props are above.
- `<NumberField.Group>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<NumberField.Input>` draws a `<input>`.
- `<NumberField.Increment>` draws a `<button>`.
- `<NumberField.Decrement>` draws a `<button>`.
- `<NumberField.ScrubArea>` draws a `<span>`.
    - `direction?: "horizontal" | "vertical"`: The way the pointer is dragged to change the number: `"horizontal"`, where right is more, or `"vertical"`, where up is more. Default `"horizontal"`.
    - `pixelSensitivity?: number`: How many pixels the pointer moves before the number changes: more is slower. Default 2.
    - `teleportDistance?: number`: How far past the scrub area's edges the drawn cursor goes before it comes back in at the other side, in pixels, half of it at each edge. Default: the edges of the window.
- `<NumberField.ScrubAreaCursor>` draws a `<span>`.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: Groups the number field's parts.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when the number cannot be changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when a number must be given.
    - `data-touched`: Present once focus has left the input.
    - `data-dirty`: Present while the number is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Present while there is a number.
    - `data-focused`: Present while the input has focus.
    - `data-scrubbing`: Present while the number is dragged from its scrub area.
    - `data-valid`: In a field: present once the number was checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: In a field: present while the number is wrong.
- group: What holds the input and its buttons, as one control.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when the number cannot be changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when a number must be given.
    - `data-touched`: Present once focus has left the input.
    - `data-dirty`: Present while the number is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Present while there is a number.
    - `data-focused`: Present while the input has focus.
    - `data-scrubbing`: Present while the number is dragged from its scrub area.
    - `data-valid`: In a field: present once the number was checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: In a field: present while the number is wrong.
- input: The text input: it takes what its locale writes a number with.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when the number cannot be changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when a number must be given.
    - `data-touched`: Present once focus has left the input.
    - `data-dirty`: Present while the number is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Present while there is a number.
    - `data-focused`: Present while the input has focus.
    - `data-scrubbing`: Present while the number is dragged from its scrub area.
    - `data-valid`: In a field: present once the number was checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: In a field: present while the number is wrong.
- increment: A button that steps the number up. Held, it goes on.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when the number cannot be changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when a number must be given.
    - `data-touched`: Present once focus has left the input.
    - `data-dirty`: Present while the number is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Present while there is a number.
    - `data-focused`: Present while the input has focus.
    - `data-scrubbing`: Present while the number is dragged from its scrub area.
    - `data-valid`: In a field: present once the number was checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: In a field: present while the number is wrong.
- decrement: A button that steps the number down. Held, it goes on.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when the number cannot be changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when a number must be given.
    - `data-touched`: Present once focus has left the input.
    - `data-dirty`: Present while the number is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Present while there is a number.
    - `data-focused`: Present while the input has focus.
    - `data-scrubbing`: Present while the number is dragged from its scrub area.
    - `data-valid`: In a field: present once the number was checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: In a field: present while the number is wrong.
- scrubArea: An area that is pressed and dragged to change the number: the field's label, as a rule. It takes `direction`, `pixelSensitivity` and `teleportDistance`. A mouse's pointer is locked for the drag where the browser has that (not in Safari); a finger drags as it is.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when the number cannot be changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when a number must be given.
    - `data-touched`: Present once focus has left the input.
    - `data-dirty`: Present while the number is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Present while there is a number.
    - `data-focused`: Present while the input has focus.
    - `data-scrubbing`: Present while the number is dragged from its scrub area.
    - `data-valid`: In a field: present once the number was checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: In a field: present while the number is wrong.
- scrubAreaCursor: What is drawn in place of the pointer while it is locked for a drag: in the page only then, at the end of `<body>`, placed by the component.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when the number cannot be changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when a number must be given.
    - `data-touched`: Present once focus has left the input.
    - `data-dirty`: Present while the number is not the one it started with.
    - `data-filled`: Present while there is a number.
    - `data-focused`: Present while the input has focus.
    - `data-scrubbing`: Present while the number is dragged from its scrub area.
    - `data-valid`: In a field: present once the number was checked and found right.
    - `data-invalid`: In a field: present while the number is wrong.

### Otp

```
import { Otp } from "@kirana-ui/react/otp"
```

Parts: `<Otp.Root>`, `<Otp.Input>`, `<Otp.Group>`, `<Otp.Slot>`, `<Otp.Separator>`, `<Otp.Caret>`.

Anatomy:

```
<Otp.Root>
  <Otp.Input>
  <Otp.Group> (repeated)
    <Otp.Slot> (repeated)
      <Otp.Caret>
  <Otp.Separator> (repeated)
```

Props of its root:

- `length?: number`: How many characters the code has. Default: 6.
- `value?: string`: The characters typed so far, when the caller holds them.
- `defaultValue?: string`: The characters it starts with, when the caller does not hold `value`. Read once. Default `""`.
- `onValueChange?: (value: string, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Heard as the characters are about to change: `details.cancel()` keeps them as they were.
- `onComplete?: (value: string) => void`: Every character is in: the moment to send the code.
- `mode?: "numeric" | "alphabetic" | "alphanumeric" | "text"`: What a character may be: a digit (`numeric`), a letter (`alphabetic`, `a` to `z` either case), either (`alphanumeric`), or anything but white space (`text`). It also says which keyboard a phone shows: the digits' for `numeric`, letters' otherwise. Default: `numeric`, on purpose: a one-time code is digits, and its keyboard is then the one to type them on.
- `pattern?: string`: What else a character may be: a regular expression, as text, that one character must match whole (`"[A-F0-9]"`), in place of `mode`'s rule. Text, as an attribute can only be, so it is given the same way on every framework and on a custom element. With a pattern, `mode` only says the keyboard, and defaults to `text`.
- `disabled?: boolean`: Disabled: it cannot be changed.
- `name?: string`: With a name, the code is submitted with the form around it.
- `form?: string`: The id of the form the input belongs to, when it is not inside it.
- `id?: string`: The id of its input, not of the root: a `<label for>` names it.

Each part, and its own props:

- `<Otp.Root>` draws a `<div>`. Its props are above.
- `<Otp.Input>` draws a `<input>`.
- `<Otp.Group>` draws a `<div>`. Cells that are drawn together.
- `<Otp.Slot>` draws a `<div>`.
    - `index: number`: Required. Which character of the code it shows, from 0.
- `<Otp.Separator>` draws a `<div>`. A mark between groups of cells.
- `<Otp.Caret>` draws a `<div>`. A caret drawn in the active cell while it is empty.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: The code: the input and its cells.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-focused`: Present while the input has focus.
    - `data-complete`: Present when every character is in.
- input: The one input the code is typed in. A design lays it over the cells, unseen.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- slot: One cell of the code.
    - `data-index`: The cell's place, from 0.
    - `data-active`: Present on the cell the next character goes in, or that is selected.
    - `data-filled`: Present when the cell has its character.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.

### Pagination

```
import { Pagination } from "@kirana-ui/react/pagination"
```

Parts: `<Pagination.Root>`, `<Pagination.Items>`, `<Pagination.Item>`, `<Pagination.Ellipsis>`, `<Pagination.Previous>`, `<Pagination.Next>`.

Anatomy:

```
<Pagination.Root>
  <Pagination.Items>
    <Pagination.Item> (repeated)
    <Pagination.Ellipsis> (repeated)
  <Pagination.Previous>
  <Pagination.Next>
```

Props of its root:

- `page?: number`: The page shown, from 1.
- `defaultPage?: number`: The page it starts at, when the caller does not hold `page`. Read once. Default `1`.
- `onPageChange?: (page: number, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Heard as another page is about to be shown: `details.cancel()` keeps the page as it was.
- `count: number`: Required. How many items there are in all.
- `pageSize?: number`: How many items a page holds. Default 10.
- `siblingCount?: number`: How many pages are listed each side of the one shown. Default 1.
- `boundaryCount?: number`: How many pages are always listed at each end. Default 1.
- `disabled?: boolean`: Disabled: no page can be gone to.

Each part, and its own props:

- `<Pagination.Root>` draws a `<nav>`. Its props are above.
- `<Pagination.Items>` draws no element. The row's entries, pages and the gaps between them: each is given to draw.
    - `children: (entry: PaginationEntry) => ReactNode`: Required. Draws one entry, once for each: a page, or the mark for pages left out.
- `<Pagination.Item>` draws a `<button>`.
    - `page: number`: Required. The page it goes to, from 1.
- `<Pagination.Ellipsis>` draws a `<span>`. The mark for pages that are left out of the row.
- `<Pagination.Previous>` draws a `<button>`.
- `<Pagination.Next>` draws a `<button>`.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: The pages of a list, as a navigation.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- item: A page: pressed, it is the one shown.
    - `data-selected`: Present on the page that is shown.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- previous: Goes to the page before.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- next: Goes to the page after.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.

### Popover

```
import { Popover } from "@kirana-ui/react/popover"
```

Parts: `<Popover.Root>`, `<Popover.Trigger>`, `<Popover.Portal>`, `<Popover.Backdrop>`, `<Popover.Positioner>`, `<Popover.Popup>`, `<Popover.Arrow>`, `<Popover.Title>`, `<Popover.Description>`, `<Popover.Close>`.

Anatomy:

```
<Popover.Root>
  <Popover.Trigger>
  <Popover.Portal>
    <Popover.Backdrop>
    <Popover.Positioner>
      <Popover.Popup>
        <Popover.Title>
        <Popover.Description>
        <Popover.Close>
        <Popover.Arrow>
```

Props of its root:

- `open?: boolean`: Whether it is open, when the caller holds it.
- `defaultOpen?: boolean`: Whether it starts open, when the caller does not hold `open`. Read once.
- `onOpenChange?: (open: boolean, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Heard as it is about to open or close: `details.cancel()` keeps it as it was.
- `modal?: boolean | "trap-focus"`: What the page behind it may do while it is open. `false` (the default): everything. `true`: nothing, the page is inert and does not scroll, and Tab stays inside the popover. `"trap-focus"`: Tab stays inside the popover, and the page can still be pressed and scrolled. A popover the pointer opened holds nothing until it is pressed. Read as it opens.

Each part, and its own props:

- `<Popover.Root>` draws no element. Holds the popover: whether it is open. Its props are above.
- `<Popover.Trigger>` draws a `<button>`.
    - `openOnHover?: boolean`: Whether the pointer resting on the trigger opens the popover too. A press and the keyboard still open it, and a press on one the pointer opened keeps it open. Default `false`.
    - `delay?: number`: How long the pointer rests on the trigger before the popover opens, in milliseconds. Default 300.
    - `closeDelay?: number`: How long after the pointer leaves a popover it opened closes, in milliseconds. Default 0.
- `<Popover.Portal>` draws no element. Draws no element of its own: its children at the end of `<body>`, or where a `PortalProvider` says.
- `<Popover.Backdrop>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<Popover.Positioner>` draws a `<div>`. Takes the positioner options ("Positioner options", above).
- `<Popover.Popup>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<Popover.Arrow>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<Popover.Title>` draws a `<h2>`. The heading that names the popover.
- `<Popover.Description>` draws a `<p>`. The text that describes the popover.
- `<Popover.Close>` draws a `<button>`. A button that closes the popover.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- trigger: The button that opens the popover, and what it is placed against.
    - `data-popup-open`: Present when the popover is open.
- backdrop: A layer over the page behind the popover.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
- positioner: Places the popup against the trigger. It carries the geometry.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `--anchor-width`: The anchor's width.
    - `--anchor-height`: The anchor's height.
    - `--available-width`: The width between the anchor and the edge of the viewport.
    - `--available-height`: The height between the anchor and the edge of the viewport.
    - `--transform-origin`: The point of the popup nearest its anchor, to scale from.
- popup: The popover itself.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
- arrow: An element that points at the trigger, placed along the popup's edge.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `data-uncentered`: Present when the popup was pushed along its edge, so the arrow is not at the trigger's centre.

### Progress

```
import { Progress } from "@kirana-ui/react/progress"
```

Parts: `<Progress.Root>`, `<Progress.Track>`, `<Progress.Indicator>`, `<Progress.Value>`, `<Progress.Label>`.

Anatomy:

```
<Progress.Root>
  <Progress.Track>
    <Progress.Indicator>
  <Progress.Value>
  <Progress.Label>
```

Props of its root:

- `value: number | null`: Required. The value. For a progress bar, `null` is "under way, how far is not known".
- `min?: number`: Default 0.
- `max?: number`: Default 100.
- `format?: Intl.NumberFormatOptions`: How the value is written; a percentage of the range by default.
- `locale?: string`: The language the value is written in; the page's by default.
- `getAriaValueText?: (text: string | undefined, value: number | null) => string`: What assistive technology reads for the value, when the written value is not enough.

Each part, and its own props:

- `<Progress.Root>` draws a `<div>`. Its props are above.
- `<Progress.Track>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<Progress.Indicator>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<Progress.Value>` draws a `<span>`.
    - `children?: (text: string | undefined) => ReactNode`: Draws something else than the written value: it is given the text, `undefined` while there is none.
- `<Progress.Label>` draws a `<span>`.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: The progress bar: it says the value to assistive technology.
    - `data-progressing`: Present while the task is under way.
    - `data-complete`: Present once the value has reached the end of the range.
    - `data-indeterminate`: Present while how far the task has come is not known.
- track: The whole range.
    - `data-progressing`: Present while the task is under way.
    - `data-complete`: Present once the value has reached the end of the range.
    - `data-indeterminate`: Present while how far the task has come is not known.
- indicator: The filled part: its width is the value's share of the range.
    - `data-progressing`: Present while the task is under way.
    - `data-complete`: Present once the value has reached the end of the range.
    - `data-indeterminate`: Present while how far the task has come is not known.
- value: The value, written.
    - `data-progressing`: Present while the task is under way.
    - `data-complete`: Present once the value has reached the end of the range.
    - `data-indeterminate`: Present while how far the task has come is not known.
- label: The bar's name.
    - `data-progressing`: Present while the task is under way.
    - `data-complete`: Present once the value has reached the end of the range.
    - `data-indeterminate`: Present while how far the task has come is not known.

### QrCode

```
import { QrCode } from "@kirana-ui/react/qr-code"
```

Parts: `<QrCode.Root>`, `<QrCode.Frame>`, `<QrCode.Pattern>`.

Anatomy:

```
<QrCode.Root>
  <QrCode.Frame>
    <QrCode.Pattern>
```

Props of its root:

- `value: string`: Required. What the code says: a link, a text. Written as UTF-8.
- `correction?: QrCorrection`: How much of it may be lost and still be read. Default: `"M"`.

Each part, and its own props:

- `<QrCode.Root>` draws a `<div>`. Its props are above.
- `<QrCode.Frame>` draws a `<svg>`. The drawing: an `<svg>` a module to the unit.
- `<QrCode.Pattern>` draws a `<path>`. The dark modules: one `<path>`, filled by the design.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: What holds the code.
    - `data-invalid`: Present when the value is longer than a code holds.

### RadioGroup

```
import { RadioGroup } from "@kirana-ui/react/radio-group"
```

Parts: `<RadioGroup.Root>`, `<RadioGroup.Item>`, `<RadioGroup.Indicator>`.

Anatomy:

```
<RadioGroup.Root>
  <RadioGroup.Item> (repeated)
    <RadioGroup.Indicator>
```

Props of its root:

- `value?: Value | null`: The chosen value; `null` is "none".
- `defaultValue?: Value | null`: The value it starts with, when the caller does not hold `value`. Read once.
- `onValueChange?: (value: Value | null, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: `null` only when a form's reset takes the group back to "none".
- `disabled?: boolean`: Disables every item of the group.
- `readOnly?: boolean`: Shown as it is, focusable, not changeable.
- `required?: boolean`: Needed: in a `Field`, choosing none is then invalid.
- `name?: string`: With a name, the chosen value is submitted with the form around the group.
- `form?: string`: The id of the form the control belongs to, when it is not inside it.

Each part, and its own props:

- `<RadioGroup.Root>` draws a `<div>`. Generic: `<Value = unknown>`. `Value` is what tells an item from the others: the type of `value`. Its props are above.
- `<RadioGroup.Item>` draws a `<span>`.
    - `value: unknown`: Required. What the group's value is while this item is the chosen one.
    - `disabled?: boolean`: Disables this item: it cannot be chosen.
    - `id?: string`: The id of the item's native radio, unique in the page: a `<label htmlFor>` names it.
- `<RadioGroup.Indicator>` draws a `<span>`.
    - `keepMounted?: boolean`: Keeps the mark in the page while its item is not the chosen one.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: Groups the items: one of them is chosen at most.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when the form needs it.
- item: One choice. It holds a hidden native radio, which a form and a label reach: the item's `id` (`kpId` on Angular, `kui-id` on a custom element) is the radio's, which a `<label for>` names.
    - `data-checked`: Present when it is checked.
    - `data-unchecked`: Present when it is not checked.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when the form needs it.
- indicator: The mark. In the page while its item is the chosen one.
    - `data-checked`: Present when it is checked.
    - `data-unchecked`: Present when it is not checked.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when the form needs it.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.

### Resizable

```
import { Resizable } from "@kirana-ui/react/resizable"
```

Parts: `<Resizable.Group>`, `<Resizable.Panel>`, `<Resizable.Handle>`.

Anatomy:

```
<Resizable.Group>
  <Resizable.Panel> (repeated)
  <Resizable.Handle> (repeated)
```

Props of its root:

- `orientation?: Orientation`: Whether the panels are side by side (the default) or one over the other.
- `onSizesChange?: (sizes: number[], details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Heard as the panels are resized: each panel's share, in the page's order, summing to 100.
- `keyboardStep?: number`: How far an arrow key moves a handle, in hundredths of the group. Default: 10.
- `disabled?: boolean`: Disabled: the handles cannot be dragged or moved with the keyboard.

Each part, and its own props:

- `<Resizable.Group>` draws a `<div>`. Its props are above.
- `<Resizable.Panel>` draws a `<div>`.
    - `defaultSize?: number`: Its share to begin with, in hundredths of the group. Either every panel gives one or none does (they are then equal).
    - `minSize?: number`: The least it can be made. Default: 0.
    - `maxSize?: number`: The most it can be made. Default: 100.
- `<Resizable.Handle>` draws a `<div>`.
    - `disabled?: boolean`: Disables this handle: it cannot be dragged or moved with the keyboard.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- group: The panels and the bars between them. A design lays it out as a flex box: `display: flex`, and `flex-direction: column` when it is vertical. A group in a panel that is a flex box itself takes `min-width: 0` and `min-height: 0`, or what it holds widens the panel.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: Whether the panels are side by side or one over the other.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- panel: One panel. It carries its share of the group, written as its `flex` with `min-width: 0` and `min-height: 0`, so what it holds cannot keep it past its share. Its `overflow` is the design's.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: Whether the panels are side by side or one over the other.
    - `--panel-size`: The panel's share, in hundredths of the group.
- handle: The bar between two panels: dragged, or moved with the arrows. A design gives it its thickness and `flex-shrink: 0`, so the panels do not squeeze it.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: Whether the panels are side by side or one over the other.
    - `data-dragging`: Present while the bar is dragged.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.

### ScrollArea

```
import { ScrollArea } from "@kirana-ui/react/scroll-area"
```

Parts: `<ScrollArea.Root>`, `<ScrollArea.Viewport>`, `<ScrollArea.Content>`, `<ScrollArea.Scrollbar>`, `<ScrollArea.Thumb>`, `<ScrollArea.Corner>`.

Anatomy:

```
<ScrollArea.Root>
  <ScrollArea.Viewport>
    <ScrollArea.Content> (optional)
    <ScrollArea.Scrollbar> (repeated, as above)
  <ScrollArea.Scrollbar> (repeated)
    <ScrollArea.Thumb>
  <ScrollArea.Corner>
```

Each part, and its own props:

- `<ScrollArea.Root>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<ScrollArea.Viewport>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<ScrollArea.Content>` draws a `<div>`. A box around what is scrolled, as wide as what it holds. Not needed to measure: the viewport's children are watched as they are. For content whose own box does not grow with what is in it (a block holding a wider table, or bare text).
- `<ScrollArea.Scrollbar>` draws a `<div>`.
    - `orientation?: Orientation`: Which way it scrolls. Default: `vertical`.
    - `keepMounted?: boolean`: In the page even while there is nothing to scroll its way.
- `<ScrollArea.Thumb>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<ScrollArea.Corner>` draws a `<div>`. The square where the two scrollbars meet, placed there.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: The area. It holds the viewport and the scrollbars, which the library places against it: a design gives a scrollbar its thickness and draws it, and places nothing.
    - `data-has-overflow-x`: Present when there is more to see sideways.
    - `data-has-overflow-y`: Present when there is more to see up or down.
    - `data-scrolling`: Present while it is being scrolled, and a moment after.
    - `data-hovering`: Present while the pointer is over the area.
    - `--scroll-area-corner-width`: The width of the corner: the vertical scrollbar's, while both scrollbars and the corner are in the page.
    - `--scroll-area-corner-height`: The height of the corner: the horizontal scrollbar's, while both scrollbars and the corner are in the page.
- viewport: The element that scrolls.
    - `data-has-overflow-x`: Present when there is more to see sideways.
    - `data-has-overflow-y`: Present when there is more to see up or down.
    - `data-scrolling`: Present while it is being scrolled, and a moment after.
- scrollbar: A scrollbar's track, placed along its edge of the area. In the page while there is something to scroll its way.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: Which way the scrollbar scrolls.
    - `data-hovering`: Present while the pointer is over the area.
    - `data-scrolling`: Present while the area is scrolled its way.
    - `--scroll-area-thumb-height`: A vertical thumb's height.
    - `--scroll-area-thumb-width`: A horizontal thumb's width.
- thumb: The part of a scrollbar that shows where the view is, and can be dragged. As long as its scrollbar's variable says.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: Which way the scrollbar scrolls.

### Select

```
import { Select } from "@kirana-ui/react/select"
```

Parts: `<Select.Root>`, `<Select.Trigger>`, `<Select.Value>`, `<Select.Portal>`, `<Select.Positioner>`, `<Select.Popup>`, `<Select.List>`, `<Select.ScrollUpArrow>`, `<Select.ScrollDownArrow>`, `<Select.Group>`, `<Select.GroupLabel>`, `<Select.Separator>`, `<Select.Item>`, `<Select.ItemText>`, `<Select.ItemIndicator>`.

Anatomy:

```
<Select.Root>
  <Select.Trigger>
    <Select.Value>
  <Select.Portal>
    <Select.Positioner>
      <Select.Popup>
        <Select.ScrollUpArrow>
        <Select.List> (optional)
          <Select.Group> (optional, repeated)
            <Select.GroupLabel>
            <Select.Item> (repeated)
              <Select.ItemText>
              <Select.ItemIndicator>
          <Select.Separator> (repeated)
        <Select.ScrollDownArrow>
```

Props of its root:

- `value?: Value | null`: The chosen value; `null` is "none".
- `defaultValue?: Value | null`: The value it starts with, when the caller does not hold `value`. Read once.
- `onValueChange?: (value: Value | null, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Heard as a value is about to be chosen: `details.cancel()` keeps it as it was.
- `open?: boolean`: Whether the list is open, when the caller holds it.
- `defaultOpen?: boolean`: Whether the list starts open, when the caller does not hold `open`. Read once.
- `onOpenChange?: (open: boolean, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Heard as the list is about to open or close: `details.cancel()` keeps it as it was.
- `disabled?: boolean`: Disabled: it cannot be changed.
- `readOnly?: boolean`: Shown as it is, focusable, not changeable: the list still opens to be read, and no item can be chosen. Its value is still submitted with the form.
- `required?: boolean`: In a field, "none" is then wrong.
- `name?: string`: With a name, the value is submitted with the form around it.
- `form?: string`: The id of the form the control belongs to, when it is not inside it.
- `items?: readonly { value: Value; label: string }[] | Readonly<Record<string, string>>`: The labels of the values, for the trigger to show before the list has ever been opened: a list of values with their labels, or, for values that are text, the labels by value (`{ apple: "Apple" }`). Not needed for the list itself: its items are read from the markup.
- `multiple?: boolean`: Several values: an item chosen is added, chosen again taken away, and the list stays open. The values are `values`, not `value`.
- `values?: readonly Value[]`: With `multiple`: the chosen values, in the order they were chosen.
- `defaultValues?: readonly Value[]`: With `multiple`: the values it starts with, when the caller does not hold `values`. Read once.
- `onValuesChange?: (values: Value[], details: ChangeDetails) => void`: With `multiple`: heard as a value is about to be added or taken away, with the values there would then be: `details.cancel()` keeps them as they were.
- `virtualized?: ListCollection`: Every row, when only some are in the page (a virtualizer draws the ones in view). Each item is then given its `index`.

Each part, and its own props:

- `<Select.Root>` draws no element. Generic: `<Value = unknown>`. `Value` is what tells an item from the others: the type of `value`, and of `values`' entries. Its props are above.
- `<Select.Trigger>` draws a `<button>`.
- `<Select.Value>` draws a `<span>`. Generic: `<Chosen = unknown>`.
    - `placeholder?: ReactNode`: Shown while nothing is chosen.
    - `children?: ReactNode | (( value: Chosen, label: Chosen extends readonly unknown[] ? readonly string[] : string | undefined ) => ReactNode)`: What to show in place of the label. A function is given the value and its label (`null` and `undefined` while nothing is chosen); with `multiple`, the values and their labels, in the items' order. Its first parameter's type says which: `(values: string[], labels) => …`.
- `<Select.Portal>` draws no element. Draws no element of its own: its children at the end of `<body>`, or where a `PortalProvider` says.
- `<Select.Positioner>` draws a `<div>`. Takes the positioner options ("Positioner options", above).
    - `alignItemWithTrigger?: boolean`: The list opens over its trigger, the chosen item's text on the trigger's own, where there is room and unless a finger opened it.
- `<Select.Popup>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<Select.List>` draws a `<div>`. The items' own box inside the popup, when the popup holds more than its items: the listbox, and what scrolls.
- `<Select.ScrollUpArrow>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<Select.ScrollDownArrow>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<Select.Group>` draws a `<div>`. Items that belong together, named by their label.
- `<Select.GroupLabel>` draws a `<div>`. The name of a group. Outside a group it is plain text, and names nothing.
- `<Select.Separator>` draws a `<div>`. A line between groups.
- `<Select.Item>` draws a `<div>`.
    - `value: unknown`: Required. What the select's value is while this item is chosen.
    - `disabled?: boolean`: Disables this item: it cannot be chosen, and the arrows pass over it.
    - `label?: string`: What typeahead matches and the trigger shows; the item's text when left out.
    - `index?: number`: Its place among all the rows, in a virtualized list.
- `<Select.ItemText>` draws a `<span>`. The item's name: what the trigger shows once it is chosen.
- `<Select.ItemIndicator>` draws a `<span>`. A mark an item shows while it is chosen.
    - `keepMounted?: boolean`: Keeps the mark in the page while its item is not chosen.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- trigger: The button that shows the value and opens the list.
    - `data-popup-open`: Present when the list is open.
    - `data-placeholder`: Present while nothing is chosen.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
- value: The chosen value's label, or the placeholder. With several values, their labels with commas between.
    - `data-placeholder`: Present while nothing is chosen.
- positioner: Places the list against the trigger. It carries the geometry.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end | none"`: The side of the trigger it is on, after any flip; `none` when it lies over the trigger.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `--anchor-width`: The anchor's width.
    - `--anchor-height`: The anchor's height.
    - `--available-width`: The width between the anchor and the edge of the viewport.
    - `--available-height`: The height between the anchor and the edge of the viewport.
    - `--transform-origin`: The point of the popup nearest its anchor, to scale from.
- scrollUpArrow: In the page while there is more of the list above: it scrolls the list while the pointer moves over it.
    - `data-direction="up | down"`: The way it scrolls the list.
    - `data-visible`: Present while there is more of the list its way.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end | none"`: The side of the trigger the list is on; `none` when it lies over the trigger.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
- scrollDownArrow: In the page while there is more of the list below: it scrolls the list while the pointer moves over it.
    - `data-direction="up | down"`: The way it scrolls the list.
    - `data-visible`: Present while there is more of the list its way.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end | none"`: The side of the trigger the list is on; `none` when it lies over the trigger.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
- popup: The list of items.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
- item: One choice in the list.
    - `data-selected`: Present on the chosen item, or on each of several.
    - `data-highlighted`: Present on the item the pointer or the keyboard is on.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.

### Separator

```
import { Separator } from "@kirana-ui/react/separator"
```

Props:

- `orientation?: Orientation`: Whether the line lies across (the default) or stands upright: what a screen reader is told.

`<Separator>` draws a `<div>`.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: The line.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: The way the line runs.

### Slider

```
import { Slider } from "@kirana-ui/react/slider"
```

Parts: `<Slider.Root>`, `<Slider.Value>`, `<Slider.Control>`, `<Slider.Track>`, `<Slider.Indicator>`, `<Slider.Thumb>`.

Anatomy:

```
<Slider.Root>
  <Slider.Value>
  <Slider.Control>
    <Slider.Track>
      <Slider.Indicator>
      <Slider.Thumb> (repeated)
```

Props of its root:

- `value?: Value`: The value, when the caller holds it: a number, or a list of numbers for a range.
- `defaultValue?: Value`: Read once. Default `min`.
- `onValueChange?: (value: SliderTold<Value>, details: SliderChangeDetails) => void`: Each step of a drag and each key.
- `onValueCommitted?: (value: SliderTold<Value>, details: SliderChangeDetails) => void`: When the pointer lets go, and after each key: the value to save.
- `min?: number`: Default 0.
- `max?: number`: Default 100.
- `step?: number`: Default 1.
- `largeStep?: number`: What Page Up, Page Down and an arrow with Shift move by. Default 10.
- `minStepsBetweenValues?: number`: How many steps two thumbs of a range stay apart. Default 0.
- `orientation?: Orientation`: Whether the track lies across (the default) or stands upright: the arrows that move a thumb follow.
- `thumbAlignment?: "center" | "edge" | "edge-client-only"`: Where a thumb is at the ends of its range. `"center"` (the default): its centre on the control's edge, so half of it lies outside. `"edge"`: its edge on the control's edge, so it stays inside. `"edge-client-only"` is the same here: nothing waits for the browser.
- `disabled?: boolean`: Disabled: it cannot be changed.
- `readOnly?: boolean`: Shown as it is, focusable, not changeable: no key and no pointer moves a thumb, and its value is still submitted with the form.
- `name?: string`: With a name, each thumb's value is submitted with the form around the slider.
- `form?: string`: The id of the form the control belongs to, when it is not inside it.
- `format?: Intl.NumberFormatOptions`: How a value is written.
- `locale?: string`: The language a value is written in; the page's by default.
- `getAriaValueText?: (text: string, value: number, index: number) => string`: What assistive technology reads for a thumb, when the written value is not enough.

Each part, and its own props:

- `<Slider.Root>` draws a `<div>`. Generic: `<Value extends SliderValue = SliderValue>`. `Value` is what the slider is given, `value` or `defaultValue`: a number for one thumb, a list for a range. What `onValueChange` and `onValueCommitted` are told is the same kind. Its props are above.
- `<Slider.Value>` draws a `<output>`.
    - `children?: (text: string, values: readonly number[]) => ReactNode`: Draws something else than the written value: it is given the text, and each thumb's value.
- `<Slider.Control>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<Slider.Track>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<Slider.Indicator>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<Slider.Thumb>` draws a `<div>`.
    - `index?: number`: Which value of a range the thumb is, from 0. A thumb that is given none takes its place among the slider's thumbs, in the order they are written.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: Groups the slider's parts.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: The way the track runs.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-dragging`: Present while a pointer holds a thumb.
- value: The value, written.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: The way the track runs.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-dragging`: Present while a pointer holds a thumb.
- control: What a pointer presses and drags on. It holds the track and the thumbs.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: The way the track runs.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-dragging`: Present while a pointer holds a thumb.
- track: The whole range.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: The way the track runs.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-dragging`: Present while a pointer holds a thumb.
- indicator: The filled part: up to the thumb, or from the first thumb to the last. Its place and length are written on it.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: The way the track runs.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-dragging`: Present while a pointer holds a thumb.
    - `--start-position`: With thumbs that stay inside the control: where the filled part starts, or with one thumb where it ends.
    - `--relative-size`: With thumbs that stay inside the control and a range: the filled part's length.
- thumb: What is dragged, and what the keyboard moves: a slider to assistive technology. Its place on the track is written on it. It holds a hidden input, which a form reads. A thumb that is given no `index` is the value at its place among the slider's thumbs, in the order they are written.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: The way the track runs.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-dragging`: Present while a pointer holds a thumb.
    - `data-index`: Which thumb it is, from 0.
    - `--position`: With thumbs that stay inside the control: where the thumb's centre is.

### Switch

```
import { Switch } from "@kirana-ui/react/switch"
```

Parts: `<Switch.Root>`, `<Switch.Thumb>`.

Anatomy:

```
<Switch.Root>
  <Switch.Thumb>
```

Props of its root:

- `checked?: boolean`: Whether it is checked, when the caller holds it.
- `defaultChecked?: boolean`: Read once.
- `onCheckedChange?: (checked: boolean, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Heard as it is about to be checked or unchecked: `details.cancel()` keeps it as it was.
- `disabled?: boolean`: Disabled: it cannot be changed.
- `readOnly?: boolean`: Shown as it is, focusable, not changeable.
- `required?: boolean`: Needed: in a `Field`, leaving it unchecked is then invalid.
- `name?: string`: With a name, the control is submitted with the form around it when it is checked.
- `form?: string`: The id of the form the control belongs to, when it is not inside it.
- `value?: string`: What is submitted. Default `"on"`, as a native checkbox's.
- `id?: string`: The id of the switch's hidden native checkbox, not of the switch: a `<label for>` names it. Inside a `Field`, that input takes the field's id instead.

Each part, and its own props:

- `<Switch.Root>` draws a `<span>`. Its props are above.
- `<Switch.Thumb>` draws a `<span>`.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: The track. It holds a hidden native checkbox, which a form and a label reach.
    - `data-checked`: Present when it is checked.
    - `data-unchecked`: Present when it is not checked.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when the form needs it.
- thumb: The knob that moves along the track.
    - `data-checked`: Present when it is checked.
    - `data-unchecked`: Present when it is not checked.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-readonly`: Present when it can be read but not changed.
    - `data-required`: Present when the form needs it.

### Tabs

```
import { Tabs } from "@kirana-ui/react/tabs"
```

Parts: `<Tabs.Root>`, `<Tabs.List>`, `<Tabs.Tab>`, `<Tabs.Indicator>`, `<Tabs.Panel>`.

Anatomy:

```
<Tabs.Root>
  <Tabs.List>
    <Tabs.Tab> (repeated)
    <Tabs.Indicator>
  <Tabs.Panel> (repeated)
```

Props of its root:

- `value?: Value | null`: The active tab's value; `null` is "none".
- `defaultValue?: Value | null`: Read once. Without one, the first tab that can be chosen is, once the page is there.
- `onValueChange?: (value: Value, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Told a tab's own value, never `null`: tabs do not go back to none.
- `orientation?: Orientation`: Whether the tabs are laid out across (the default) or down: the arrows that move between them follow.

Each part, and its own props:

- `<Tabs.Root>` draws a `<div>`. Generic: `<Value = unknown>`. `Value` is what tells a tab from the others: the type of `value`. Its props are above.
- `<Tabs.List>` draws a `<div>`.
    - `activateOnFocus?: boolean`: Whether moving focus onto a tab with the arrows activates it. Default `false`.
    - `loop?: boolean`: Whether the arrows wrap from the last tab to the first. Default `true`.
- `<Tabs.Tab>` draws a `<button>`.
    - `value: unknown`: Required. What the tabs' value is while this tab is the active one.
    - `disabled?: boolean`: Disables this tab: it cannot be chosen.
- `<Tabs.Indicator>` draws a `<span>`.
- `<Tabs.Panel>` draws a `<div>`.
    - `value: unknown`: Required. The value of the tab this is the panel of.
    - `keepMounted?: boolean`: Keeps the panel in the page, `hidden`, while its tab is not the active one.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: Groups the tabs and their panels.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: The way the tabs are laid out.
    - `data-activation-direction="left | right | up | down | none"`: Where the newly active tab is from the one before, for a panel or a mark that slides.
- list: The row of tabs. The arrows move between them.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: The way the tabs are laid out.
    - `data-activation-direction="left | right | up | down | none"`: Where the newly active tab is from the one before, for a panel or a mark that slides.
- tab: A button that shows its panel.
    - `data-active`: Present on the tab whose panel is shown.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: The way the tabs are laid out.
- indicator: A mark for the active tab: it carries that tab's position and size.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: The way the tabs are laid out.
    - `data-activation-direction="left | right | up | down | none"`: Where the newly active tab is from the one before, for a panel or a mark that slides.
    - `--active-tab-left`: The active tab's distance from the list's left edge.
    - `--active-tab-right`: The active tab's distance from the list's right edge.
    - `--active-tab-top`: The active tab's distance from the list's top edge.
    - `--active-tab-bottom`: The active tab's distance from the list's bottom edge.
    - `--active-tab-width`: The active tab's width.
    - `--active-tab-height`: The active tab's height.
- panel: A tab's content. In the page while its tab is active, and through its exit.
    - `data-hidden`: Present while its tab is not the active one.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: The way the tabs are laid out.
    - `data-activation-direction="left | right | up | down | none"`: Where the newly active tab is from the one before, for a panel or a mark that slides.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.

### Toast

```
import { Toast } from "@kirana-ui/react/toast"
```

Parts: `<Toast.Viewport>`, `<Toast.List>`, `<Toast.Root>`, `<Toast.Content>`, `<Toast.Title>`, `<Toast.Description>`, `<Toast.Close>`, `<Toast.Action>`.

Anatomy:

```
<Toast.Viewport>
  <Toast.List>
    <Toast.Root> (repeated)
      <Toast.Content> (optional)
        <Toast.Title>
        <Toast.Description>
      <Toast.Close>
      <Toast.Action>
```

Props of its root:

- `toast: ToastRecord`: Required. The toast it draws: the one `Toast.List` gave its child.

Each part, and its own props:

- `<Toast.Viewport>` draws a `<div>`.
    - `toaster: Toaster<Content>`: Required. The toaster whose toasts are drawn: one made with `createToaster()`. Needed.
    - `label?: string`: What the region of toasts is called, for assistive technology. Default: `"Notifications"`.
    - `hotkey?: string`: The key that takes focus to the toasts. Default: `"F6"`.
    - `swipeDirection?: "left" | "right" | "up" | "down"`: The way a toast is dragged to close it. Default: `"right"`.
- `<Toast.List>` draws no element. The toasts in the page: each is given to draw its root.
    - `children: (toast: ToastRecord) => ReactNode`: Required. Draws one toast, once for each, the newest first: a `Toast.Root` given it as `toast`.
- `<Toast.Root>` draws a `<div>`. Its props are above.
- `<Toast.Content>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<Toast.Title>` draws a `<div>`. What the toast is called: the title it was added with, when nothing else is written in it.
- `<Toast.Description>` draws a `<div>`. What the toast says: the description it was added with, when nothing else is written in it.
- `<Toast.Close>` draws a `<button>`. Closes the toast.
- `<Toast.Action>` draws a `<button>`. A button of the toast's own: the action it was added with, when nothing else is written in it. Pressing it closes the toast too, unless the action refuses.

A page's toasts are a toaster's, made once in a module: `import { createToaster } from "@kirana-ui/react"`, then `export const toaster = createToaster(options)` (`ToasterOptions`, under "Types"). The viewport is given it, and anything on the page adds to it: `toaster.add({ title, description, action, priority })`, `toaster.update(id, options)`, `toaster.dismiss(id)`, `toaster.promise(promise, { loading, success, error })`. What each takes and gives back is `Toaster`, `ToastOptions`, `ToastActionOptions` and `ToastRecord` under "Types".

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- viewport: Where the toasts are drawn: a region that is always in the page.
    - `data-expanded`: Present while the pointer or focus is on the stack: the toasts are spread out, and wait.
    - `--toast-frontmost-height`: The height of the newest toast.
- root: One toast.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
    - `data-expanded`: Present while the pointer or focus is on the stack: the toasts are spread out, and wait.
    - `data-type`: The kind the toast was added as.
    - `data-limited`: Present on a toast behind as many as are shown at once.
    - `data-swiping`: Present while the toast is dragged.
    - `data-swipe-direction="left | right | up | down"`: The way the toast was dragged out, once it has been.
    - `--toast-index`: Its place in the stack: 0 for the newest.
    - `--toast-height`: Its height.
    - `--toast-offset-y`: The height of the toasts in front of it.
    - `--toast-swipe-movement-x`: How far it has been dragged across.
    - `--toast-swipe-movement-y`: How far it has been dragged up or down.
- content: What holds a toast's contents, when the design sizes the toast itself.
    - `data-behind`: Present on a toast that is behind the newest.
    - `data-expanded`: Present while the pointer or focus is on the stack: the toasts are spread out, and wait.

### Toggle

```
import { Toggle } from "@kirana-ui/react/toggle"
```

Props:

- `pressed?: boolean`: Whether it is pressed, when the caller holds it.
- `defaultPressed?: boolean`: Read once.
- `onPressedChange?: (pressed: boolean, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Heard as it is about to be pressed or released: `details.cancel()` keeps it as it was.
- `disabled?: boolean`: Disabled: a press does nothing.
- `value?: unknown`: In a toggle group: what the group's value holds while this one is pressed.

`<Toggle>` draws a `<button>`.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: The button. It stays pressed until it is pressed again.
    - `data-pressed`: Present while it is pressed.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.

### ToggleGroup

```
import { ToggleGroup } from "@kirana-ui/react/toggle-group"
```

Props:

- `value?: readonly Value[]`: The values of the pressed toggles: none, one, or with `multiple` several.
- `defaultValue?: readonly Value[]`: The values pressed at the start, when the caller does not hold `value`. Read once.
- `onValueChange?: (value: Value[], details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Heard as a toggle is about to be pressed or released, with the values that would then be pressed: `details.cancel()` keeps them as they were.
- `multiple?: boolean`: Whether more than one can be pressed at a time.
- `disabled?: boolean`: Disables every toggle of the group.
- `orientation?: Orientation`: Whether the toggles are laid out across (the default) or down: the arrows that move between them follow.
- `loop?: boolean`: Whether the arrows go round from the last toggle to the first. Default: they do.

`<ToggleGroup>` draws a `<div>`. Generic: `<Value = unknown>`. `Value` is what tells a toggle from the others: the type of `value`'s entries.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: The group. A toggle inside it with a `value` is one of its toggles.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: Whether its toggles are in a row or a column.
    - `data-multiple`: Present when several can be pressed at a time.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.

### Toolbar

```
import { Toolbar } from "@kirana-ui/react/toolbar"
```

Parts: `<Toolbar.Root>`, `<Toolbar.Button>`, `<Toolbar.Link>`, `<Toolbar.Input>`, `<Toolbar.Group>`, `<Toolbar.Separator>`.

Anatomy:

```
<Toolbar.Root>
  <Toolbar.Group> (optional, repeated)
    <Toolbar.Button> (repeated)
    <Toolbar.Link> (repeated)
    <Toolbar.Input> (repeated)
  <Toolbar.Separator> (repeated)
```

Props of its root:

- `orientation?: Orientation`: Whether the controls are laid out across (the default) or down: the arrows that move between them follow.
- `loop?: boolean`: Whether the arrows go round from the last item to the first. Default: they do.
- `disabled?: boolean`: Disables every control of the toolbar.

Each part, and its own props:

- `<Toolbar.Root>` draws a `<div>`. Its props are above.
- `<Toolbar.Button>` draws a `<button>`.
    - `disabled?: boolean`: Disables this control.
- `<Toolbar.Link>` draws a `<a>`.
- `<Toolbar.Input>` draws a `<input>`.
    - `disabled?: boolean`: Disables this control.
- `<Toolbar.Group>` draws a `<div>`.
    - `disabled?: boolean`: Disables this control.
- `<Toolbar.Separator>` draws a `<div>`.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- root: The toolbar. It is one stop for Tab.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: Whether the toolbar is a row or a column.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- button: A button of the toolbar.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: Whether the toolbar is a row or a column.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- link: A link of the toolbar.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: Whether the toolbar is a row or a column.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- input: A text input of the toolbar. The arrows are its own until the caret is at an end.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: Whether the toolbar is a row or a column.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- group: Items that belong together.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: Whether the toolbar is a row or a column.
    - `data-disabled`: Present when it is disabled.
- separator: A line between items, across the toolbar.
    - `data-orientation="horizontal | vertical"`: Whether the toolbar is a row or a column.

### Tooltip

```
import { Tooltip } from "@kirana-ui/react/tooltip"
```

Parts: `<Tooltip.Root>`, `<Tooltip.Trigger>`, `<Tooltip.Portal>`, `<Tooltip.Positioner>`, `<Tooltip.Popup>`, `<Tooltip.Arrow>`.

Anatomy:

```
<Tooltip.Root>
  <Tooltip.Trigger>
  <Tooltip.Portal>
    <Tooltip.Positioner>
      <Tooltip.Popup>
        <Tooltip.Arrow>
```

Props of its root:

- `open?: boolean`: Whether it is open, when the caller holds it.
- `defaultOpen?: boolean`: Whether it starts open, when the caller does not hold `open`. Read once.
- `onOpenChange?: (open: boolean, details: ChangeDetails) => void`: Heard as it is about to open or close: `details.cancel()` keeps it as it was.
- `delay?: number`: How long the pointer rests on the trigger before the popup opens, in milliseconds. Default `600`.
- `closeDelay?: number`: How long after the pointer leaves the popup closes, in milliseconds. Default `0`.
- `disabled?: boolean`: Disabled: the pointer and focus do not open it.

Each part, and its own props:

- `<Tooltip.Root>` draws no element. Holds the tooltip: whether it is open. Its props are above.
- `<Tooltip.Trigger>` draws a `<button>`.
    - `delay?: number`: How long the pointer rests on this trigger before the popup opens, in milliseconds.
    - `closeDelay?: number`: How long after the pointer leaves this trigger's popup closes, in milliseconds.
- `<Tooltip.Portal>` draws no element. Draws no element of its own: its children at the end of `<body>`, or where a `PortalProvider` says.
- `<Tooltip.Positioner>` draws a `<div>`. Takes the positioner options ("Positioner options", above).
- `<Tooltip.Popup>` draws a `<div>`.
- `<Tooltip.Arrow>` draws a `<div>`.

Attributes and CSS variables, by part:

- trigger: The element the tooltip describes.
    - `data-popup-open`: Present when the tooltip is open.
- positioner: Places the popup against the trigger. It carries the geometry.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `--anchor-width`: The anchor's width.
    - `--anchor-height`: The anchor's height.
    - `--available-width`: The width between the anchor and the edge of the viewport.
    - `--available-height`: The height between the anchor and the edge of the viewport.
    - `--transform-origin`: The point of the popup nearest its anchor, to scale from.
- popup: The tooltip itself.
    - `data-open`: Present when it is open.
    - `data-closed`: Present when it is closed.
    - `data-starting-style`: Present for the first style of its entrance: what it animates in from.
    - `data-ending-style`: Present through its exit: what it animates out to. It leaves the page when the motion ends.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `data-instant="delay | focus | dismiss"`: Present when it opened or closed without its usual wait, for a design that skips the motion then.
- arrow: An element that points at the trigger, placed along the popup's edge.
    - `data-side="top | right | bottom | left | inline-start | inline-end"`: The side of the anchor it is on, after any flip. Asked for as `inline-start` or `inline-end`, it says one of those two when it is beside its anchor.
    - `data-align="start | center | end"`: How it is aligned with the anchor.
    - `data-uncentered`: Present when the popup was pushed along its edge, so the arrow is not at the trigger's centre.
